item.title: Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s record 141-game 20-point streak snapped in win over Nuggets
item.description: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s record 141-game 20-point streak snapped in win over Nuggets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ’s historic scoring run has finally come to an end , but the Oklahoma City Thunder still found a way to win. The 28-year-old scored 17 points in the Thunder’s 96-84 home win over the Denver Nuggets on Thursday night at Paycom Center. That snapped his NBA-record streak of 141 straight regular-season games with at least 20 points. The run began on Nov. 1, 2024, early in the 2024-25 season, and stretched for nearly two full years, per Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints . Gilgeous-Alexander also became a two-time MVP during that stretch , cementing his place among the league’s elite. He rewrote the record books along the way, tying Wilt Chamberlain’s longtime mark of 126 straight 20-point games on March 9, 2026, against these same Nuggets. He made that night even more memorable by hitting a game-winning 3-pointer in a 129-126 victory. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Three days later, the four-time NBA All-Star officially passed Chamberlain with his 127th straight game in a 104-102 win over the Boston Celtics. Chamberlain’s streak had stood for more than six decades. It started on Oct. 19, 1961, and ended on Jan. 20, 1963, when he was ejected four minutes into a game against the St. Louis Hawks. Gilgeous-Alexander then kept the run going for another 14 games , pushing the record to 141 before Thursday’s game against Denver. That number may be tough for anyone to touch for a long time, given how rare it is for a player to stay healthy and productive across that many games. The two-time MVP opened the new season in typical fashion. He dropped 32 points in a 116-104 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday . The streak was a reflection of how consistent SGA has been as one of the league’s most reliable scorers. Night after night, he found a way to reach 20 points regardless of the opponent or game situation. Thursday’s game showed that the Thunder can still get it done when their superstar has an off night by his standards. Oklahoma City improved to 2-0 with the win over a Western Conference rival. For Gilgeous-Alexander, the end of the streak is unlikely to slow him down. He will look to start a new run when the Thunder take the floor again, with plenty of the regular season still ahead. His 141-game mark now stands as the new benchmark. Related: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s rise challenges the NBA’s rush to judge young stars Related: Thunder news: Sam Presti used The Tortoise and the Hare to turn Shai Gilgeous-Alexander into an MVP, NBA champion

item.title: Asian football endorses Infantino re-election as FIFA president
item.description: President of the Asian Football Confederation speaking last year (Mohd RASFAN) The head of the Asian Football Confederation on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president following fierce criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the AFC when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing. The AFC in August had joined UEFA (Europe) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term. "I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president," said Sheikh Salman, in a significant boost to Infantino's prospects. "I think you've visited a lot of countries in Asia. I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent. "I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear." Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: "Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past. "But let's not relate the two things together. We need to move forward... football is strongest when we work together." Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March. The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18. No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him so far, despite outspoken condemnation especially from Europe. Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his relationship with US President Donald Trump. bur-pst/hol

item.title: Andre Onana: Man United loanee’s stock rises as he keeps fourth clean sheet in five matches
item.description: Andre Onana: Man United loanee’s stock rises as he keeps fourth clean sheet in five matches Manchester United had one player on loan action on Thursday evening. Andre Onana The Cameroonian keeper has been in good form this season for Trabzonspor. The Turkish side have won five matches in a row and are just three points from the top of the league. They are also going well in the Conference League, having won two out of two matches. The Turkish side took care of business last night, defeating Scottish side Heart of Midlothian 2-0 at home in spite of receiving a red card in the match. The match Onana kept a clean sheet in the match, his fourth in five matches for the Turkish club. In a quiet match for the Cameroonian, he only had one save to make as Hearts struggled to make an impact on the game. He saved well from a free kick in the 10th minute from Cláudio Braga. Onana also had little to do to protect his box as he was not needed to make any high claims or to punch the ball out, as the visitors rarely threatened the home side’s goal. His passing was quite on point, as he completed 86% of his passes and 40% of his long ball attempts as he tried to push his side up the pitch. The keeper lost the ball six times in the match but carried the ball forwards 20 times as he left his area. Onana also recovered the ball twice in the match and did not need to compete in any ground duels. The keeper will next be in action when Trabzonspor travel to face Çaykur Rizespor on Monday evening. Andre Onana stats vs Hearts Featured image Carl Recine via Getty Images online polls

item.title: It’s time to take Bears seriously as Super Bowl contenders after convincing win over Patriots
item.description: It’s time to take Bears seriously as Super Bowl contenders after convincing win over Patriots appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears are making it increasingly difficult to dismiss them as an entertaining upstart. Right now, this team is beginning to look like a legitimate threat in the NFC. Thursday night’s 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots was not a flawless performance. Still, it was another compelling example of the Bears finding answers when the pressure intensified. Caleb Williams delivered a statement performance. The supporting cast produced explosive plays. Cairo Santos supplied a clutch finish. At 5-2, Chicago has earned more than compliments for its improvement. It deserves to enter the Super Bowl conversation. Difference-maker The biggest reason for optimism is Williams. He continues to show signs of becoming the franchise quarterback Chicago has long needed. Against New England, he completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. His 119.3 passer rating reflected a poised performance. Williams was particularly effective attacking downfield. He punished coverage mistakes instead of allowing New England to dictate the terms of the game. His ability to locate open receivers and deliver accurate throws helped Chicago generate chunk plays. Just as importantly, he protected the football well. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Of course, Williams still has room to improve, especially in sustaining that level of execution against defenses capable of disguising coverages and applying consistent pressure. That said, performances like Thursday’s offer tangible evidence that his development is translating into winning football. Offensive arsenal Williams is not carrying this team alone. Chicago’s most encouraging development is the variety of ways it can hurt opposing defenses. This has made the offense far more difficult to contain than a unit dependent on one featured receiver. Luther Burden III was the headline performer against New England. He turned four receptions into 130 yards and a touchdown. His explosive scoring play on third-and-17 demonstrated how quickly Chicago can punish a defensive mistake. Colston Loveland adds another dimension. His touchdown threat from the tight end position gives Williams a target capable of exploiting space. Meanwhile, Rome Odunze can stretch coverage on the perimeter. In addition, D’Andre Swift supplies a credible ground threat and a receiving option out of the backfield. item.content:encoded: It’s time to take Bears seriously as Super Bowl contenders after convincing win over Patriots appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears are making it increasingly difficult to dismiss them as an entertaining upstart. Right now, this team is beginning to look like a legitimate threat in the NFC. Thursday night’s 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots was not a flawless performance. Still, it was another compelling example of the Bears finding answers when the pressure intensified. Caleb Williams delivered a statement performance. The supporting cast produced explosive plays. Cairo Santos supplied a clutch finish. At 5-2, Chicago has earned more than compliments for its improvement. It deserves to enter the Super Bowl conversation. Difference-maker The biggest reason for optimism is Williams. He continues to show signs of becoming the franchise quarterback Chicago has long needed. Against New England, he completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. His 119.3 passer rating reflected a poised performance. Williams was particularly effective attacking downfield. He punished coverage mistakes instead of allowing New England to dictate the terms of the game. His ability to locate open receivers and deliver accurate throws helped Chicago generate chunk plays. Just as importantly, he protected the football well. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Of course, Williams still has room to improve, especially in sustaining that level of execution against defenses capable of disguising coverages and applying consistent pressure. That said, performances like Thursday’s offer tangible evidence that his development is translating into winning football. Offensive arsenal Williams is not carrying this team alone. Chicago’s most encouraging development is the variety of ways it can hurt opposing defenses. This has made the offense far more difficult to contain than a unit dependent on one featured receiver. Luther Burden III was the headline performer against New England. He turned four receptions into 130 yards and a touchdown. His explosive scoring play on third-and-17 demonstrated how quickly Chicago can punish a defensive mistake. Colston Loveland adds another dimension. His touchdown threat from the tight end position gives Williams a target capable of exploiting space. Meanwhile, Rome Odunze can stretch coverage on the perimeter. In addition, D’Andre Swift supplies a credible ground threat and a receiving option out of the backfield. Chicago can lean on its passing game in a shootout or use Swift to help manage the clock when protecting a lead. Head coach Ben Johnson deserves credit for building an offense that can create mismatches. The Bears still need greater week-to-week consistency, but the ingredients for a dangerous postseason attack are clearly taking shape. Finishing close games Super Bowl contenders must execute when games become tense, possessions become precious, and one mistake can determine the outcome. Chicago demonstrated that composure against New England. The Patriots kept fighting behind Drake Maye, who threw for 321 yards . Yet the Bears made the decisive late-game plays. Santos drilled a career-long, 58-yard field goal to extend the advantage to nine points with 1:34 remaining. New England eventually pulled within six, but Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick to secure the victory. That finish was significant because it showed Chicago could withstand a late push without allowing the game to slip away. Santos delivered under pressure, while the team handled the final moments well enough to preserve the result. Now, there are surely still concerns. The Bears allowed 24 points, surrendered several explosive plays, and needed a late special-teams contribution to create breathing room. Better opponents will test those defensive vulnerabilities more severely. Still, winning close games is a skill. The Bears are gaining valuable experience in exactly those situations. Entering the conversation Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Nobody should hand Chicago a Lombardi Trophy in October — far from it. As things stand, the NFC remains crowded at the top. Also, the Bears have not yet demonstrated that they can sustain their best football over an entire season. Despite that, their trajectory is difficult to ignore. Williams is playing with growing confidence. Johnson has assembled a versatile offense. Chicago is showing an ability to deliver in decisive moments. Those are foundational qualities for a serious contender. The next challenge is consistency. The Bears must prove that Thursday night’s performance was not an isolated peak. If they can do that, they will have a legitimate chance to compete with the conference’s best. Right now, Chicago has already earned the right to be taken seriously. The Bears making a case that their Super Bowl window may be opening sooner than anyone expected. Related: Caleb Williams calls out Richard Sherman for doubting Bears after big Patriots win Related: Bears hold off Patriots for big win on TNF to get to 5-2

item.title: UFC 333 weigh-in video: Volkanovski vs. Evloev
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC At the UFC 333 weigh-ins, all 28 fighters on Saturday’s UFC fight card step on the scale Friday morning in Abu Dhabi. Watch ceremonial weigh-ins above and highlights of the main and co-main event fighters below. In the main event, Alexander Volkanovski defends his featherweight title against the undefeated Movsar Evloev. Both fighters need to weigh 145 pounds or less for the title fight. The co-main event sees bantamweight champion Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili face off for a third time, with both men earning a win in the series. Yan became a two-time champion this past December with a thrilling decision win over Dvalishvili in their rematch at UFC 323. Both fighters need to weigh 135 pounds or less for the title fight. Nothing new for The Champ 👑 @AlexVolkanovski weighs in at 144.5 lbs! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE OCT 24 at 2pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/JsoLPWZSAt — UFC (@ufc) October 23, 2026 Nothing will stand in his way 💪 @MovsarUFC weighs in at 145 lbs! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE OCT 24 at 2pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/PhfJCZbTAT — UFC (@ufc) October 23, 2026 No Mercy 😤 @PetrYanUFC weighs in at 135 lbs! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE OCT 24 at 2pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/hSVjHCaib6 — UFC (@ufc) October 23, 2026 Redemption on his mind 👊 @MerabDvalishvil weighs in at 135 lbs! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE OCT 24 at 2pmET on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/DWLEVvWDnz — UFC (@ufc) October 23, 2026 The UFC 333 official weigh-ins kick off at 1 a.m. ET / 10 p.m. PT late Thursday evening. The UFC 333 ceremonial weigh-ins will be at 10 a.m. ET / 7 a.m. PT on Friday. Check out UFC 333 weigh-in results below. Main Card (Paramount+ 2 p.m. ET) Alexander Volkanovski (144.5) vs. Movsar Evloev (145) Petr Yan (135) vs. Merab Dvalishvili (135) Lone’er Kavanagh vs. Ramazan Temirov (126) Alexander Volkov vs. Rizvan Kuniev Aaron Pico (145.5) vs. Losene Keita (146) Preliminary Card (Paramount+ at 12 p.m. ET) Azamat Murzakanov (206) vs. Dominick Reyes Nikita Krylov vs. Abdul Rakhman Yakhyaev (206) Abus Magomedov (185.5) vs. Cam Rowston (185) Grant Dawson (156) vs. Nurullo Aliev (155) Early Prelims (Paramount+ at 10 a.m. ET) Colby Thicknesse (135.5) vs. Asaf Chopurov Abubakar Vagaev (185.5) vs. Jacob Malkoun (186) Bolaji Oki (146) vs. Daniel Santos (146) Kody Steele (156) vs. Noah Gugnon (156) Iasmin Lucindo (115) vs. Nicolle Caliari (120.5)* *missed weight

item.title: Where to watch Timberwolves vs. Magic today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Friday NBA game
item.description: Where to watch Timberwolves vs. Magic today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Friday NBA game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Timberwolves will continue a grueling opening week on the road with a matchup against the Magic on Friday night. The T-Wolves will leave South Beach and head north to Orlando with hopes of snagging another away win. Minnesota is adjusting well to a new faster-paced dynamic, and the combination of Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball is already showing promise for a strong 2026-27 campaign. The Magic have a tough first-week schedule as well, facing the Hawks , Timberwolves and Knicks in quick succession. Given the strength of these teams, Orlando will be relying heavily on Paolo Banchero to put points on the board. There will also be pressure on Franz Wagner to perform, though the guard has been battling shoulder soreness in recent games. Can Minnesota come away with a 2-0 start? Here's everything you need to know about Timberwolves vs. Magic, including TV channel and streaming options for the NBA game. Where to watch Timberwolves vs. Magic today TV channels: WRDQ TV27 (Orlando) Live streams: DAZN (Timberwolves) The Timberwolves-Magic game will be televised locally on WRDQ TV27 in Orlando. Those in the Minnesota area can watch live and on-demand with DAZN . DAZN is Minnesota's new direct-to-consumer media partner, set to air preseason and regular-season games along with additional Timberwolves content all season long ( read more here ). All games not selected for exclusive national broadcast by one of the league's partners will be available to stream live and on-demand with DAZN, which offers a free trial for new subscribers. What time is Timberwolves vs. Magic today? Date: Friday, Oct. 23 Time: 7 p.m. ET | 6 p.m. CT The Timberwolves vs. Magic game is set to tip off Friday at 7 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Kia Center in Orlando, FL. Timberwolves schedule 2026-27 Here are Minnesota's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 23 at Magic 7 p.m. Oct. 25 vs. Raptors 7 p.m. Oct. 26 at Cavs 7 p.m. Oct. 28 vs. Warriors 8 p.m. Oct. 30 vs. Clippers 8 p.m. Magic schedule 2026-27 Here are Orlando's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 23 vs. Timberwolves 7 p.m. Oct. 25 at Knicks 7 p.m. Oct. 28 at Raptors 7:30 p.m. Oct. 23 at Raptors 7:30 p.m. Nov. 1 vs. Celtics 3:30 p.m. Related Links Latest NBA news and rumors Full NBA schedule, scores How to bet on the NBA The GOAT Debate: Michael Jordan vs. LeBron James

item.title: Serge Gnabry feeling confident after Bayern Munich’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal
item.description: (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Serge Gnabry believes Bayern Munich can take confidence from their 2-2 draw with Arsenal, even though the German champions were left frustrated after conceding a late equalizer. Bayern appeared to have taken control after scoring their second goal, but Arsenal fought back to earn a share of the points. Gnabry acknowledged the disappointment while recognizing the quality of the opposition. “I thought we had th em after we scored the second goal, but they managed to equalize. It was a fair result. It was a game betw een two top teams. We can live with that,” Gnabry said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). The Bayern attacker also offered his assessment of where Vincent Kompany’s side currently stands in the Europe an pecking order, expressing confidence that Bayern belongs among the continent’s best teams. “I think we’re among the top. In the end, what matters is the period between February and May. Of course, we have to put ourselves in a good position by finishing in the top 8, and then we’ll see.” Gnabry’s comments highlight Bayern’s bigger objective this season. Performing well during the league phase is importan t, but the ultimate test will come in the knockout rounds, when the biggest trophies are decided. Bayern have shown th ey can compete with Europe’s elite. Now, the challenge is to turn that potential into results when it matters most. Join the conversation! item.title: 'LeBricked a few': Skip Bayless reacts to LeBron James' performance after 76ers beat Cavaliers
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James helped the Philadelphia 76ers beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106, but Skip Bayless still had a lot to say about the veteran. All eyes were on The King as he made his Philly debut on Thursday night, but it wasn’t a great start for him or his team. However, the Sixers’ quality showed later in the game, and they pulled off an incredible comeback to go 2-0 this season. Bayless complained about James’ performance early on, but he gave him his flowers after the game – well, sort of. Skip Bayless reacts to LeBron James and 76ers’ win over Cavaliers It wasn’t a dominant start by the Sixers against the Cavaliers by any means on Thursday night. There was some sloppy play early on by the hosts, and Bayless, unsurprisingly, pointed the finger at James a couple of times while the game was still going on. His first tweet read: “Come on, LeBron, you can’t set the tone for a big national-TV game against your original team – your Sixers home opener – with three turnovers in the 8 minutes you played in the 1st quarter. You’re better than that.” Bayless added 35 minutes later on X : “LeBron: 5 points and FIVE TURNOVERS at half as Sixers trail 69-45. Come on, man.” The 76ers then got their act together and overturned a 29-point deficit to win the game in the end. Bayless hailed the Sixers for their show of class and also appeared to praise James, with a few jibes along the way. He said in a video on X: “Oh, Lord, have mercy. What a display of superior talent by the Philadelphia 76ers with one of the greatest comebacks in Sixers history. From 29 down to win by eight over the visiting Cavaliers flexing and flaunting the talent. “Maxey, 32 and Embiid, 28, and Jaylen Brown, 21. And that guy, 23, that LeBron guy, first year in Philly, home opener in Philly, shook off his five first-half turnovers that put them in the hole or at least helped to, and started playing a little basketball in the second half. “Actually went along for a great ride. Wound up with 17 and 9 rebounds. Didn’t shoot it well from three. LeBricked a few, as usual, one of four. I’d like to see 10 assists, but he had five. “Because when it was time, Tyrese Maxey just said: ‘No, I got it.’ And he was dribbling the ball up the floor and initiating the offence most of the night. “All I know is this is the best team in the East. Knicks, you are officially in trouble. Enjoy, LeBron.” That’s probably as much of a compliment as LeBron will get from Bayless after a game like that, but the latter could be right about one thing: The Sixers may well be the best team in the East right now. Read more: ‘Ring us already’ – 76ers fans react after 114-106 comeback win over Cavaliers LeBron James issues sarcastic one-line response to Donald Trump after he called him a ‘disgrace’ Trump staffer Britt McHenry caught on video throwing drink at fan during Wizards game

item.title: Quarterback Jayden Garcia leads Churchill over LEE to keep playoff hopes alive
item.description: Churchill quarterback Jayden Garcia (1) reacts after making a fourth quarter touchdown against the LEE Volunteers at Jerry Comalander Stadium in San Antonio, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. The Chargers defeated the Volunteers 44-16. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whether it was through the air or on the ground, it didn't matter. LEE had no answers for Churchill quarterback Jayden Garcia. The senior racked up 337 total yards and four touchdowns as the Chargers cruised past the Volunteers 44-16 Thursday at Comalander Stadium. "His ability to extend plays is something that's a nice fallback plan when things aren't going well," Churchill coach Nate Shaw said. "And then to have the ability to create and extend plays, it gets us out of tough situations." A 49-yard punt return from senior Henry Kalisky set up a Churchill score on its opening drive. On the Chargers' first play from scrimmage, senior Kalobe Rond cut through the center of the Volunteers' defense, breaking a tackle en route to a 10-yard rushing touchdown. But a missed extra point left the score at 6-0. On the ensuing drive, LEE quarterback Troy Sosa hit senior Fabian Martinez for a 57-yard gain. The Volunteers then rushed five consecutive times before senior Tahrie Chandler punched in the 2-yard touchdown, giving LEE a 7-6 lead with 6:20 remaining in the first quarter. View this post on Instagram A post shared by San Antonio High School Sports (@sanantoniohss) The Chargers offense punched back, quickly driving inside the LEE 10-yard line. It took four attempts, but junior Justin Mason got through the Vols' line on a 2-yard touchdown off a direct snap to put the Chargers back ahead 13-7. Garcia got in on the ground game early in the second quarter. The senior scampered for 41 yards into the red zone, and two plays later, he called his own number for the score. Dropping back to pass, Garcia scanned the field. With nothing open, he darted through the center of his offensive line before cutting left and turning the corner for a 12-yard touchdown. Mason converted the 2-point rush for Churchill, putting the Chargers up 21-7. "It's just preparing," Garcia said. "We watched the film. Our coaches put a great game plan together, so we knew what we had to do." LEE kicker Angel Pena connected on a 26-yard field goal on the Volunteers' next drive, cutting the deficit to 11 points with 6:00 left in the half. Churchill appeared primed to extend its lead on its next possession, but the Chargers fumbled on the LEE 1-yard line. The Volunteers returned the favor, though, and shanked a 34-yard field goal attempt on their ensuing drive, leaving the score at 21-10 heading into halftime. Garcia found his rhythm through the air in the second half. He connected with senior Timothy Mizell for two touchdowns to help Churchill break open the game. Churchill's Jayden Garcia (1) makes a pass during the second quarter against the LEE Volunteers at Jerry Comalander Stadium in San Antonio, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. The Chargers defeated the Volunteers 44-16. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) A botched snap for a safety put the Chargers up 20 with 6:02 in the third. Garcia later scored his second rushing touchdown of the night, securing a key victory that keeps the Chargers alive in the playoff race. "I just saw a team that wants to win," Garcia said. item.title: Enzo Maresca pledges to restore Phil Foden as England's finest after Manchester City star hits hat-trick form
item.description: Manchester City v AEK Athens - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has opened up on his commitment to helping Phil Foden recapture the world-class form that once made him the envy of European football. The Italian tactician believes it is his personal responsibility to guide the 26-year-old back to the pinnacle of the game following a difficult period at the Etihad Stadium. Foden bouncing back for City Foden is experiencing a rapid revival at Manchester City after serving a domestic suspension . The 26-year-old attacker has registered four goals in his last two outings, highlighted by a midweek hat-trick against AEK Athens . This sudden burst of form has reignited discussions about an international recall, following his omission from England's World Cup squad . Maresca has made Foden's rehabilitation a priority since arriving at the Etihad Stadium this summer. The Italian manager held early interventions with the forward to rebuild his confidence and reaffirm his value to the squad. A manager's duty to his star Manchester City v AEK Athens - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 Maresca explained that he took immediate action to support the England international upon taking the managerial reins. "Since we started, I sat down with Phil two or three times - especially at the beginning - just to show him, I don't know if love is the right word to use, but to show him how important he is," Maresca revealed. "I know Phil from years ago, so I know how good he is," he added. "For different reasons, the last few years he was not good enough but I think when you have players like Phil available you are a better team because it's a matter of improving players. For me, it's my duty to try to help him to be one of the best players in England again." Finding the balance with Cherki Beyond Foden, Maresca is actively working to refine 23-year-old playmaker Rayan Cherki. The Frenchman has dazzled recently, scoring superb goals against Liverpool and AEK. However, Maresca insists Cherki must improve his positional discipline to maximise his immense talent. "In this moment Rayan is one of the best players in Europe," Maresca noted. "When he is in the right position - that means when we are able to find him between the lines - he's always dangerous. Sometimes, because he loves the ball and he loves to move a lot, most of the time he is in the wrong position, but when he is in the right position he is always a weapon for us." Speaking ahead of Aston Villa clash on Saturday, Maresca drew comparisons to legends he played alongside, like Alessandro Del Piero and Zinedine Zidane. "After 35 years in football I am quite lucky that I have seen many things," he said. "Rayan has many good things but it's just a matter of balance. item.title: BBC: Man Utd start identifying Carrick replacements despite ‘business as usual’ claim with three leading candidates
item.description: BBC: Man Utd start identifying Carrick replacements despite ‘business as usual’ claim with three leading candidates Manchester United are reportedly already compiling a shortlist of Michael Carrick replacements after Wednesday’s defeat to Como. Although the club have suggested it’s ‘business as usual’ in the lead-up to Sunday’s clash with Bournemouth, BBC Sport’s Simon Stone suggests they’re scouring the market for potential successors. Who could succeed Carrick in the Old Trafford hot seat? (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) He claims that Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann ‘have their eyes’ on the potential United vacancy. As things stand, Carrick is due to speak to the press at 1.30pm this afternoon for his pre-match press conference, and he’ll undoubtedly be put on the spot regarding his future. United are without a win in their last seven games across all competitions – their longest winless run since they stretched to eight matches in December 2015. They last tasted victory in the Premier League in August when overturning Ipswich Town 5-2 at Old Trafford, and they have since drawn four times and lost to Manchester City. The aftermath of Como 4-1 United (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Carrick’s tactics came into question by none other than his skipper, Bruno Fernandes , at full-time in Italy. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he expressed. Further pressed on whether he believed the manager got said tactics wrong , he responded: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Carrick seemed to hit back at Fernandes himself when speaking to the media, saying: “We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that. “It’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.” Michael Carrick responded to Bruno Fernandes' post-match comments criticising the tactics. pic.twitter.com/RpJLlaEstb Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.content:encoded: BBC: Man Utd start identifying Carrick replacements despite ‘business as usual’ claim with three leading candidates Manchester United are reportedly already compiling a shortlist of Michael Carrick replacements after Wednesday’s defeat to Como. Although the club have suggested it’s ‘business as usual’ in the lead-up to Sunday’s clash with Bournemouth, BBC Sport’s Simon Stone suggests they’re scouring the market for potential successors. Who could succeed Carrick in the Old Trafford hot seat? (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) He claims that Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann ‘have their eyes’ on the potential United vacancy. As things stand, Carrick is due to speak to the press at 1.30pm this afternoon for his pre-match press conference, and he’ll undoubtedly be put on the spot regarding his future. United are without a win in their last seven games across all competitions – their longest winless run since they stretched to eight matches in December 2015. They last tasted victory in the Premier League in August when overturning Ipswich Town 5-2 at Old Trafford, and they have since drawn four times and lost to Manchester City. The aftermath of Como 4-1 United (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Carrick’s tactics came into question by none other than his skipper, Bruno Fernandes , at full-time in Italy. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he expressed. Further pressed on whether he believed the manager got said tactics wrong , he responded: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Carrick seemed to hit back at Fernandes himself when speaking to the media, saying: “We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that. “It’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.” Michael Carrick responded to Bruno Fernandes' post-match comments criticising the tactics. pic.twitter.com/RpJLlaEstb Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: MotoGP Australian GP: Marco Bezzecchi leads Aprilia 1-2-4-5 in Friday Practice
item.description: Motorsport photo Marco Bezzecchi topped Practice for the Australian Grand Prix on Friday, as Aprilia emerged as the manufacturer to beat at the start of the Phillip Island weekend. Bezzecchi, fresh off his victory in Indonesia a fortnight ago, stormed to the top with a blistering time of 1m26.775s, edging out the satellite Trackhouse bike of Raul Fernandez by just under a tenth of a second. Marc Marquez was the only Ducati rider to challenge the RS-GPs, finishing third-quickest after topping FP1 earlier this morning. Points leader Jorge Martin wound up in fifth, albeit 0.255s down on his team-mate's pace. At the start of the hour-long session, Marquez set the early benchmark on the factory Ducati, posting a time of 1m28.209s to lead from LCR’s Johann Zarco. Practice was red-flagged before the first 10 minutes had elapsed after Bezzecchi crashed at Turn 4, scattering debris across the track. The incident began when the Italian struck the back of Alex Marquez’s Gresini Ducati, losing significant bodywork in the process, before going straight into the right-hander and dropping his bike in the gravel. A second red flag followed nine minutes later due to wildlife on track, before the session resumed with 41 minutes left on the clock. Marc Marquez was again on the pace as the pitlane reopened, lapping the track in 1m27.615s to increase his advantage at the front, before Bezzecchi returned to the track on his second bike and snatched the top spot with a 1m27.374s. Full qualifying simulations began in the final 20 minutes as riders switched to the soft rear tyre, with Pedro Acosta lowering the benchmark to 1m27.208s aboard the factory KTM. A flurry of improvements followed shortly after, with Marquez moving the goalposts with the first sub-1m27s lap of the day, leaving his rivals chasing him in the closing minutes. But Aprilia rose to the fore as the final runs began, with Raul Fernandez first dislodging Marquez from the top before Bezzecchi went even quicker with a 1m26.775s. Bezzecchi's time remained unbeaten as the chequered flag was waved, with Fernandez likewise staying in second position. Marquez failed to improve on his last lap but hung on to third place, with Ai Ogura jumping to fourth late on with an identical time to the reigning world champion. Championship leader Martin managed to find more time on his final run but could only finish fifth, leaving him as the slowest of the four Aprilia riders. Meanwhile, Alex Marquez wound up sixth for Gresini despite crashing at Turn 4 with two minutes left on the clock. Tech3’s Enea Bastianini delivered a late improvement to jump to sixth place, beating the factory KTM of Pedro Acosta by just three hundredths of a second. Diogo Moreira was Honda’s top runner in ninth place, while VR46’s Fabio di Giannantonio was the last rider to secure a direct Q2 entry with 10th place. item.title: Patriots most to blame for Thursday Night Football loss to Bears
item.description: Patriots most to blame for Thursday Night Football loss to Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots had every opportunity to extend their winning streak on Thursday Night Football. Instead, they left Soldier Field with a frustrating 30-24 defeat to the Chicago Bears. Drake Maye provided enough fireworks to keep New England competitive. However, Mike Vrabel’s defense repeatedly failed to deliver when it mattered most. Against Chicago, the Patriots discovered that explosive plays and missed opportunities can erase even their most spirited efforts. Patriots fall short David Butler II-Imagn Images New England’s Week 7 showdown against Chicago featured dramatic momentum swings and several missed opportunities. Maye threw for 321 yards and two touchdowns. He also added a rushing score and connected with Rhamondre Stevenson on a spectacular 48-yard touchdown . However, Williams countered with 308 passing yards and two touchdowns. The latter repeatedly exploited New England’s coverage. Luther Burden III tormented the Patriots with 130 receiving yards. Colston Loveland added another touchdown. Cairo Santos eventually drilled a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 remaining. New England answered with a late field goal but could not recover the ensuing onside kick. Porous secondary The biggest culprit in New England’s defeat was its defensive backfield. The Patriots entered Thursday night knowing Williams possessed the arm talent to punish coverage mistakes. Unfortunately, their secondary made his job considerably easier. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Burden was particularly devastating. He turned just four receptions into 130 yards and a touchdown. His most damaging contribution came on a 58-yard catch-and-run during the first quarter. A coverage breakdown involving Christian Elliss and Charles Woods allowed him to race deep into Patriots territory. D’Andre Swift promptly finished the possession with a touchdown. That established an early advantage Chicago never relinquished. The defensive lapses continued in the second quarter. Facing third-and-17, New England had an opportunity to force a punt and prevent Chicago from extending its lead. Instead, Burden took a short completion 24 yards for another touchdown. Loveland later compounded the damage with a 12-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. He broke a tackle to restore Chicago’s double-digit advantage. These reflected a defensive unit struggling with communication, positioning, and finishing plays. Inconsistent pass rush New England’s defensive front also deserves substantial criticism. The New England Patriots had every opportunity to extend their winning streak on Thursday Night Football. Instead, they left Soldier Field with a frustrating 30-24 defeat to the Chicago Bears. Drake Maye provided enough fireworks to keep New England competitive. However, Mike Vrabel’s defense repeatedly failed to deliver when it mattered most. Against Chicago, the Patriots discovered that explosive plays and missed opportunities can erase even their most spirited efforts. Patriots fall short David Butler II-Imagn Images New England’s Week 7 showdown against Chicago featured dramatic momentum swings and several missed opportunities. Maye threw for 321 yards and two touchdowns. He also added a rushing score and connected with Rhamondre Stevenson on a spectacular 48-yard touchdown . However, Williams countered with 308 passing yards and two touchdowns. The latter repeatedly exploited New England’s coverage. Luther Burden III tormented the Patriots with 130 receiving yards. Colston Loveland added another touchdown. Cairo Santos eventually drilled a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 remaining. New England answered with a late field goal but could not recover the ensuing onside kick. Porous secondary The biggest culprit in New England’s defeat was its defensive backfield. The Patriots entered Thursday night knowing Williams possessed the arm talent to punish coverage mistakes. Unfortunately, their secondary made his job considerably easier. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Burden was particularly devastating. He turned just four receptions into 130 yards and a touchdown. His most damaging contribution came on a 58-yard catch-and-run during the first quarter. A coverage breakdown involving Christian Elliss and Charles Woods allowed him to race deep into Patriots territory. D’Andre Swift promptly finished the possession with a touchdown. That established an early advantage Chicago never relinquished. The defensive lapses continued in the second quarter. Facing third-and-17, New England had an opportunity to force a punt and prevent Chicago from extending its lead. Instead, Burden took a short completion 24 yards for another touchdown. Loveland later compounded the damage with a 12-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. He broke a tackle to restore Chicago’s double-digit advantage. These reflected a defensive unit struggling with communication, positioning, and finishing plays. Inconsistent pass rush New England’s defensive front also deserves substantial criticism. Although the Patriots generated occasional pressure, they could not consistently disrupt Williams from extending crucial possessions. Chicago’s ground game further complicated matters. Swift provided balance with 78 rushing yards and a touchdown. That forced the Patriots to respect the run rather than concentrating exclusively on Williams. There were positive moments, including a Marcus Jones sack and a third-quarter defensive stand. However, those flashes were overshadowed by an inability to string together stops. Perhaps the most frustrating sequence came in the fourth quarter when Williams connected with Rome Odunze for 21 yards on third-and-nine. That extended a possession that eventually produced Santos’ decisive 58-yard field goal. Drake Maye Maye was certainly New England’s most important offensive player Thursday night. His performance was not flawless, though. Maye repeatedly kept his team within striking distance. Nevertheless, his second-quarter interception represented a costly missed opportunity. With New England driving into Chicago’s red zone, Maye attempted a pass toward Eli Raridon in the end zone. The throw was intercepted, abruptly ending a promising possession and denying the Patriots valuable points. The mistake was particularly damaging because New England was already struggling to match Chicago’s offensive efficiency. Of course, Maye deserves credit for responding with several impressive throws, including the remarkable touchdown to Stevenson before halftime. Still, franchise quarterbacks must minimize mistakes in scoring territory, especially against opponents capable of producing explosive plays. Addressing defensive shortcomings Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images The Patriots showed resilience, but resilience alone does not win close games. Their secondary surrendered too many explosive plays. Their pass rush lacked consistency. Maye’s interception squandered a crucial scoring opportunity. Ultimately, the defensive backfield shoulders the greatest responsibility. New England’s offense produced enough points to remain competitive. However, Vrabel must demand sharper communication, cleaner tackling, and better defensive execution before the Patriots face Miami in Week 8. Otherwise, Thursday night’s disappointment could become a recurring problem rather than an isolated setback. item.title: ‘Ring us already’ – 76ers fans react after 114-106 comeback win over Cavaliers
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Philadelphia 76ers fans are already getting carried away after their team fought back from a difficult first half to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 in LeBron James’ home debut. The Sixers trailed by 24 points at one stage before turning the game around, with Tyrese Maxey leading the way with 32 points. Joel Embiid added 24 points while Jaylen Brown finished with 21 as Philadelphia improved to 2-0. James also played his part with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists, giving Sixers supporters plenty to celebrate as their new-look team continues to build momentum. Philadelphia 76ers fans react to stunning comeback against Cleveland Cavaliers The comeback has sparked plenty of excitement among Philadelphia fans, with some already daring to dream about what this team could achieve. One supporter wrote: “Ring us already” Another was encouraged by the early signs, posting: “We may have a squad.” A third fan was even more optimistic after watching Philadelphia recover from such a difficult position, writing: “Truly unbelievable win. If we can come back from that, this team might genuinely be unstoppable…” Maxey’s performance also earned plenty of praise, with one supporter highlighting the contributions of several key players. They wrote: “Absolutely incredible comeback, Maxey is the man and Jaylen just brings that solid mentality. LeBron facilitating and the on-the-floor coach, with Embiid stepping up. Hope we hold up health wise, but man; THIS IS FUN!” The result means the Sixers have started the season with two wins from two games, prompting another fan to celebrate: “2-0 GO 76ERS!!!!!” One supporter pointed to the team’s improved defence and ability to attack the basket as the turning point in the contest. They wrote: “Once the Sixers started defending with some d—- pride, Maxey got downhill, Brown attacked the gaps, and Embiid finished the job, turning a halftime humiliation into a comeback the Cavs couldn’t stop!” Another fan summed up the mood in Philadelphia with a simple message: “Philly loves a comeback story” The Sixers have made an early statement with their ability to recover from adversity, but maintaining that level of performance will be the next challenge. With Maxey producing at a high level and Embiid, Brown and James all contributing, Philadelphia fans have plenty of reasons to be excited about what comes next. item.title: Studs and duds from Bears’ 30-24 win against the Patriots
item.description: The Chicago Bears offense looks completely different with quarterback Caleb Williams on the field as evidenced in their 30-24 win over the New England Patriots. Chicago had over 400 total yards in this game for the third time this season. This was also just the second game the Bears’ offense did not commit a turnover; the other time was in their Week 3 win against the Philadelphia Eagles. Their offense started the game a little slow with only 29 yards on their opening drive. But they were able to turn that into a field goal since their drive started at midfield following a failed fourth-down conversion by the New England Patriots. Defensively, Chicago completely shut down the Patriots’ offense in the first quarter, forcing a turnover on downs followed by two punts. Things started to get going in the second quarter for New England’s offense as they were able to put up two touchdowns, including their 48-yard touchdown with three seconds left in the first half. That is the second time Chicago has given up a touchdown with three seconds or less left in the first half after giving up a touchdown to the Eagles with one second left. Here are a lot of studs and one dud from Chicago’s fifth win of the season, including Caleb Williams, who has over 300 passing yards for the second straight game and kicker Cairo Santos, who redeemed himself late. Stud: K Cairo Santos After his doink on a 53-yard field goal, it seemed like a surprising decision for the Bears to send Cairo Santos out for a 58-yarder to make it a two-possession game with 1:34 left in the game and the Patriots out of timeouts. But the decision paid off as Santos had some room left on the field goal and gave Chicago the 30-21 lead. Before this kick, his longest field goal was 55 yards, which he made back in 2023. So, not only was this the longest field goal of his career, but also the longest field goal in the history of the Chicago Bears and the third-longest field goal in the history of Soldier Field, according to the broadcast. There are a lot of people who have doubted Santos and his leg, but he made a statement with his 58-yard field goal when the Bears needed it most. Stud: WR Luther Burden III Luther Burden III did not have a single target in the second half, but still finished the game with four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. Chicago does no win this game without the amazing first half Burden had, especially his touchdown on a third and long. Burden came into this game as Chicago’s leading receiver through the first six games and now has his first game with at least 100 yards this year. It is also the second-most receiving yards Burden has had in a game in his career. He is also Chicago’s only receiver with more than one receiving touchdown after getting his second touchdown of the year. item.content:encoded: The Chicago Bears offense looks completely different with quarterback Caleb Williams on the field as evidenced in their 30-24 win over the New England Patriots. Chicago had over 400 total yards in this game for the third time this season. This was also just the second game the Bears’ offense did not commit a turnover; the other time was in their Week 3 win against the Philadelphia Eagles. Their offense started the game a little slow with only 29 yards on their opening drive. But they were able to turn that into a field goal since their drive started at midfield following a failed fourth-down conversion by the New England Patriots. Defensively, Chicago completely shut down the Patriots’ offense in the first quarter, forcing a turnover on downs followed by two punts. Things started to get going in the second quarter for New England’s offense as they were able to put up two touchdowns, including their 48-yard touchdown with three seconds left in the first half. That is the second time Chicago has given up a touchdown with three seconds or less left in the first half after giving up a touchdown to the Eagles with one second left. Here are a lot of studs and one dud from Chicago’s fifth win of the season, including Caleb Williams, who has over 300 passing yards for the second straight game and kicker Cairo Santos, who redeemed himself late. Stud: K Cairo Santos After his doink on a 53-yard field goal, it seemed like a surprising decision for the Bears to send Cairo Santos out for a 58-yarder to make it a two-possession game with 1:34 left in the game and the Patriots out of timeouts. But the decision paid off as Santos had some room left on the field goal and gave Chicago the 30-21 lead. Before this kick, his longest field goal was 55 yards, which he made back in 2023. So, not only was this the longest field goal of his career, but also the longest field goal in the history of the Chicago Bears and the third-longest field goal in the history of Soldier Field, according to the broadcast. There are a lot of people who have doubted Santos and his leg, but he made a statement with his 58-yard field goal when the Bears needed it most. Stud: WR Luther Burden III Luther Burden III did not have a single target in the second half, but still finished the game with four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. Chicago does no win this game without the amazing first half Burden had, especially his touchdown on a third and long. Burden came into this game as Chicago’s leading receiver through the first six games and now has his first game with at least 100 yards this year. It is also the second-most receiving yards Burden has had in a game in his career. He is also Chicago’s only receiver with more than one receiving touchdown after getting his second touchdown of the year. Stud: QB Caleb Williams Caleb Williams finished the game completing 66.7 percent of his passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns. He became the first quarterback for the Bears since Mitch Trubisky in 2018 to have back-to-back games with at least 300 passing yards. This is also the second game in Williams’ career where he threw for at least 300 passing yards, did not have an interception and the Bears won. He has come back from his hamstring injury looking better than he did last season, which is saying a lot. There is no doubt he is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL right now. Stud: TE Colston Loveland Colston Loveland is officially getting hot. After scoring a touchdown last week, Loveland finished the game with the most targets (12) and most receptions (seven) of anyone in this game. He also scored a touchdown for the second week in a row. The Bears meant it when they said they were going to continue to feed him the ball and it is paying off right now despite the fact that he had two drops in this game. Stud: LB D’Marco Jackson D'Marco Jackson finished the game with the second-most tackles of anyone on the team, but his interception changed the game and was ultimately one of the deciding factors in Chicago’s win. With under four minutes left in the first half, New England was driving down the field and got into the red zone. Maye took a shot at the end zone and Jackson caught the interception for the only turnover of the game. If the Patriots had scored a touchdown on that drive and gotten the extra point, they would have taken the lead. Instead, they never had a lead in this game thanks to Jackson’s interception, which was only the second of his career. Stud: RB D’Andre Swift Early in the game, D'Andre Swift took a shot to the knee from a Patriots defender and it looked like he might be out for the rest of the game. Instead, he finished the game with 22 rushing attempts for 78 yards and a touchdown, as well as four receptions for 12 yards. The Bears needed Swift to step up in this game since Kyle Monangai was out for a third straight week. He did everything Chicago needed him to and was a key part of this victory. Stud: CB Kyler Gordon Kyler Gordon may not have finished this game with three sacks, but he still had one sack early in the game and had two tackles for loss and a quarterback hit. Chicago’s defense was getting pressure on Maye all game and Gordon was a large part of that. Having him back in the lineup has clearly unlocked some schemes for defensive coordinator Dennis Allen even when he is not the one blitzing. He has been a hug addition to Chicago’s defense in the past two games. Dud: CB Jaylon Johnson The Bears might be better off just having 10 players on defense than having Jaylon Johnson on the field. He finished this game with just two tackles. But he also had a pass interference penalty late in the game and could have made the tackle on Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson right before halftime to prevent that touchdown. There was also a scramble by New England quarterback Drake Maye where he ran right by Johnson and he never even made an attempt at a tackle. He has been terrible all season. Maybe Chicago should try and trade him before the deadline, but it is unclear what teams would even want him. item.title: Jack Campbell Responds to Lions Teammate Sam LaPorta’s Comments
item.description: Jack Campbell Getty Linebacker Jack Campbell announced signing a contract extension with the Detroit Lions on Thursday. Getty Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta recently made headlines with his unfiltered comments about his frustration over the lack of meaningful progress on a contract extension beyond this season, the final year of his rookie deal. And while his comments have drawn various reactions from fans and media, his Lions teammate Jack Campbell is now weighing in with his thoughts on the matter. Jack Campbell Weighs In On Detroit Lions Teammate Sam LaPorta’s Unfiltered Comments Getty Linebacker Jack Campbell announced signing a contract extension with the Detroit Lions on Thursday. The Lions linebacker revealed that he spoke to LaPorta in the facility as if it were just any other day, and that his comments that he made while on the “Pardon My Take” podcast aren’t being discussed. “No one cares,” said Campbell on Thursday via Audacy. “No one’s like, ‘Bro, how could you say that??'” “I don’t want to overstep my boundaries,” Campbell continued. “But I know Sam’s a hell of a player, and the front office does a hell of a job, so I think it will work itself out. But it’s not, like, lingering in the locker room or anything. Everyone knows, it’s a business.” “I try to remind myself, it’s a good problem to have, but it’s not my problem,” said Campbell. “Brad does such a good job. So now it’s up to him to figure out how they can — but nowadays I feel like you can do so much stuff (with the cap). I’m not a business guy or know much about the cap and all that, but I feel like you can figure out how to restructure things and move this and that and make it not count against the cap as much … But they do have some unique decisions to make, because I’m like, we’re gonna have to figure what to do with BB, too.” LaPorta, Campbell, and the Lions face the divisional rival Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Sam LaPorta Shared Unfiltered Frustration Over The Lack Of Progress On A New Deal While making a recent appearance on the “Pardon My Take” podcast, LaPorta shared his unfiltered thoughts on not having a new contract in place. “It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt, like last year, I break my f**king back for the team, and then I’m going out there this year and I’m ballin’ and maybe they’re just not showing the love,” he said. “I’m going to continue to go do my thing and ball out,” LaPorta added, “and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jack Campbell Responds to Lions Teammate Sam LaPorta’s Comments appeared first on HEAVY .
item.content:encoded: Jack Campbell Getty Linebacker Jack Campbell announced signing a contract extension with the Detroit Lions on Thursday. Getty Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta recently made headlines with his unfiltered comments about his frustration over the lack of meaningful progress on a contract extension beyond this season, the final year of his rookie deal. And while his comments have drawn various reactions from fans and media, his Lions teammate Jack Campbell is now weighing in with his thoughts on the matter. Jack Campbell Weighs In On Detroit Lions Teammate Sam LaPorta’s Unfiltered Comments Getty Linebacker Jack Campbell announced signing a contract extension with the Detroit Lions on Thursday. The Lions linebacker revealed that he spoke to LaPorta in the facility as if it were just any other day, and that his comments that he made while on the “Pardon My Take” podcast aren’t being discussed. “No one cares,” said Campbell on Thursday via Audacy. “No one’s like, ‘Bro, how could you say that??'” “I don’t want to overstep my boundaries,” Campbell continued. “But I know Sam’s a hell of a player, and the front office does a hell of a job, so I think it will work itself out. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's historic 20-point record comes to an end at 141 games
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's historic 20-point record comes to an end at 141 games originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma City Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has proven that he is one of the best scorers of his generation with his immense skill set. He is a superstar talent with his scoring, as evidenced by his historic streak of consecutive games with 20 points or more. Unfortunately, that came to an end in the Thunder 's second game of the 2026-27 NBA season, which was against Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets . The Nuggets played against SGA well, as they limited him from scoring, but he still managed to get 17 points before he elected to sit late in the fourth quarter. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 20-point streak ends at 141 games Everyone in the NBA has become familiar with Gilgeous-Alexander and his ability to score. He can create a scoring opportunity out of nothing by making near-impossible shots at almost any angle. That helped him score 20+ points for 141 consecutive games, but that streak has finally come to an end. It was one of the most impressive achievements of any player in the modern NBA. Now, he has a chance to reset this streak, as he would love to do it all over again. He has the skill set to do so, and he has the team around him to help him do so. MORE: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gets honest about how much Russell Westbrook impacted the Thunder Gilgeous-Alexander actually had opportunities to keep the streak going when the Thunder were winning over the Nuggets. However, it seems that he decided to end the streak at 141, something that head coach Mark Daigneault admired from his superstar . "I was going to go out there, then I saw they had subbed, then I was just like, 'We should sub too.' Just like, I feel like you always treat the game with respect. God willing, I have many more games to start the streak," SGA said about the reason why he didn't try to chase the streak . Now, Gilgeous-Alexander won't have to worry about the streak. However, he will do his best to keep scoring an elite rate, and if that helps him build up another streak, it will be yet another fine achievement for the reigning two-time MVP. item.title: Fledgling roller hockey team attends Euro tournament
item.description: The international roller hockey tournament is in Spain [Supplied] A Surrey roller hockey team is to take part in a European tournament after only being founded a year ago. Farnham Roller Hockey Club's under-17s female team will represent the town at the upcoming Eurockey International Tournament in Blanes and Lloret de Mar, Spain. Lucy Collis, who coached the squad last year, said: "Playing together on the European stage for the first time is a major moment." The team were only established last season by the club, along with a senior female Premier League team. They joined the Eastern Counties female league, where they went on to win the competition in their debut year. This success, along with a "strong" application, earned them a place at the "prestigious" Eurockey contest, according to the club. "Seeing the development of our female teams has been inspiring and it brings hope for the future of women in this sport," added Collis. The team's social media manager, Rebecca Dorta, told BBC Radio Surrey roller hockey was "quite a niche sport". She said it had "sort of almost disappeared and dwindled here in the UK." Dorta added: "To see the girls and the sport flourish like this - it's great to be part of that bigger picture." She said the coaches were "really keen for the girls to get the experience, but ultimately to have a lot of fun. "I think that's really key," she added. Follow BBC Surrey on Facebook , X , and Instagram and listen to BBC Radio Surrey on Sounds . Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250. item.title: LeBron James laughs off Donald Trump criticism after 76ers’ crazy comeback vs. Cavs
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James laughs off Donald Trump criticism after 76ers’ crazy comeback vs. Cavs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LeBron James helped the Philadelphia 76ers claw back from a 29-point deficit to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers, 114-06, in their home opener at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Thursday. James had 17 points, 10 rebounds, five assists, and three steals in 33 minutes, providing all-around support to Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown, who all scored at least 20 points. Before the game, President Donald Trump went on a rant on social media, claiming James disrespected the national anthem during the 76ers’ season opener against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When a reporter asked James to comment, the 41-year-old forward gave a brief response . “Must have been a slow news day at the office,” said the four-time MVP in the video posted by PHLY Sports’ Kyle Neubeck. LeBron’s response to this after the game tonight: “must have been a slow news day at the office” https://t.co/6J3PGQ3ajG pic.twitter.com/0esGnTPOyR — Kyle Neubeck (@KyleNeubeck) October 23, 2026 It is widely known that the 80-year-old Trump does not like James, who has repeatedly criticized the business tycoon-turned-politician. Over the years, James has learned to tune out Trump, choosing not to dignify him by giving him any attention. The 76ers’ wild victory over the Cavaliers was the biggest comeback in team history in the play-by-play era. It was also the biggest comeback of James’ career. Maxey led the charge with 32 points, three rebounds, six assists, and two steals. Embiid added 24 points and seven rebounds, while Brown had 21 points, eight rebounds, and four assists. James had an accidental collision with VJ Edgecombe in the third quarter, leaving the sophomore guard with a bloody nose. The 76ers will face the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Related: 76ers’ VJ Edgecombe gives update after getting clocked in the nose by LeBron James Related: LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience in 76ers debut, and he loved every bit of it

item.title: Devils Are Leaning Into A Winning Identity With Consecutive Victories
item.description: The New Jersey Devils have hit their stride and are playing the right way early on in the season. They’ve won back-to-back games with a 4-3 win over the Colorado Avalanche and a 4-1 victory over the Anaheim Ducks while taking four of the last five games to move to 6-4 on the season. Along with the results, the Devils have played their best hockey lately. Their high-flying, skilled offense has led the way, scoring 22 goals in the last five games, but they've also stepped up defensively, especially in the last two games. The first month of the season is about finding out what the identity is and leaning into it. The Devils have found their identity and are starting to string together wins. Now, the question is whether it translates throughout the season. The Buy-In Is Noticeable The Devils needed the forwards to step up on the defensive end, especially after a few rough games to start the season. They needed the buy-in from everyone, not just the checking lines but also the skilled players. The difference is noticeable in the recent games. The Devils are blocking shots and, more importantly, are playing the shooting lanes to limit the opponent from generating many high-danger chances. “I thought defensively through the whole game; quite honestly, I thought we were quite good,” head coach Sheldon Keefe noted after the game. Devils Matchup Against The Ducks Another Test In Handling The Young Guns The Thursday night game for the Devils will show whether they can stop a skilled team from the top down, despite having a younger core. The Devils limited the Avalanche to just four shots in the first period on Tuesday night. They allowed only one to the Ducks in the latest game, helping the goaltenders start the game strong and put together great performances. “How we defend, we just make the game a lot simpler for them in front of them,” Keefe added, on the impact the defense has had on the goaltending. Goaltending Has Delivered Lately For the second game in a row, Nico Daws gave the Devils a strong start. While the 7-1 win over the New York Rangers was a dominant performance across the board, the win over the Ducks required him to step up and make a few big saves, especially late in the game. He shut the door on the Ducks to secure the 4-1 win. Devils Growing Confidence Is Noticeable & Ideally Translates All Season The Devils defeated the Avalanche 4-3 in a game that showed the swagger that the team needs for a successful season. Now, the hope is that it translates to the marathon ahead. With Jake Allen coming off a strong start of his own against the Avalanche, the Devils have found stability in the net, at least for now. They’ve won back-to-back games with a 4-3 win over the Colorado Avalanche and a 4-1 victory over the Anaheim Ducks while taking four of the last five games to move to 6-4 on the season. Their high-flying, skilled offense has led the way, scoring 22 goals in the last five games, but they've also stepped up defensively, especially in the last two games. The first month of the season is about finding out what the identity is and leaning into it. The Devils have found their identity and are starting to string together wins. Now, the question is whether it translates throughout the season. The Buy-In Is Noticeable The Devils needed the forwards to step up on the defensive end, especially after a few rough games to start the season. They needed the buy-in from everyone, not just the checking lines but also the skilled players. The difference is noticeable in the recent games. The Devils are blocking shots and, more importantly, are playing the shooting lanes to limit the opponent from generating many high-danger chances. “I thought defensively through the whole game; quite honestly, I thought we were quite good,” head coach Sheldon Keefe noted after the game. Devils Matchup Against The Ducks Another Test In Handling The Young Guns The Thursday night game for the Devils will show whether they can stop a skilled team from the top down, despite having a younger core. The Devils limited the Avalanche to just four shots in the first period on Tuesday night. They allowed only one to the Ducks in the latest game, helping the goaltenders start the game strong and put together great performances. “How we defend, we just make the game a lot simpler for them in front of them,” Keefe added, on the impact the defense has had on the goaltending. Goaltending Has Delivered Lately For the second game in a row, Nico Daws gave the Devils a strong start. While the 7-1 win over the New York Rangers was a dominant performance across the board, the win over the Ducks required him to step up and make a few big saves, especially late in the game. He shut the door on the Ducks to secure the 4-1 win. Devils Growing Confidence Is Noticeable & Ideally Translates All Season The Devils defeated the Avalanche 4-3 in a game that showed the swagger that the team needs for a successful season. Now, the hope is that it translates to the marathon ahead. With Jake Allen coming off a strong start of his own against the Avalanche, the Devils have found stability in the net, at least for now. They’ll hope it holds up, and there’s a good chance it does if the defense keeps playing at this level. The Devils Are Scoring At The Net Front A recurring issue for the Devils in previous seasons was their inability to score at the net front. They’ve struggled to get to the dirty areas and power home pucks in the crease and the slot. The skill is there, but not the goals needed to have a complete offense. Nico Hischier set the tone, with multiple goals in front of the net to start the season. He added another on Thursday as he collected a rebound and found the net for his fifth goal of the season. This Is The Best Time For The Devils To Have A “West Coast Swing” The Devils' next eight opponents are out of the conference. With the team still searching for an identity, this is a good time to face opponents they won’t see often. Now, the other forwards are following suit and scoring in the dirty areas. “For us to just find a new dimension in our game throughout all the lines. It's not just one or two lines,” Jesper Bratt noted after the win over the Ducks, a game where they scored three goals near the net. Gritsyuk Is More Confident & It Shows Gritsyuk scored again and has five goals this season. He’s always had the skill, yet the move to the Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt line has unlocked his skill offensively, with four of his five goals coming in the last five games. His skills work with Bratt and Hughes, two great skaters with plenty of skill. “We've seen the type of shot that he has, the type of player that he is,” Bratt stated, adding, “His skating, his plays with the puck, and definitely his goal-scoring touch. He just knows where to shoot. He has a great shot. We're going to tell him to keep using it.” This is Grityuk’s second season in the NHL, and he’s finding his footing in the league. He not only understands his linemates and the Devils' system, but also knows how to beat opposing defenses. It’s a growing confidence that’s made the offense tough to stop. The Lines Are Clicking But Will Adapt Over Time The opening night lineup had Anthony Mantha on the Bratt-Hughes line. The swap, which moved Mantha to the Evan Rodrigues line and Gritsyuk to the Bratt-Hughes tandem, changed the dynamics of the forward unit. Instead of different player types on the same line, the Devils now have a speed line that can gash teams and a heavier line that adds physicality. It’s allowed the Devils to come at teams in waves, and for Keefe specifically, he can lean on one line or another depending on the situation. That said, it’s a long season, and Keefe knows things will change. “Each situation is different. Each opponent is different; different situations call for different things,” he mentioned after Thursday’s win. “We've got lots of options, and it's a long season. You’re going to see lots of different people play there,” Keefe added. The Devils have depth, and it allows them to prepare for each situation. In the past five games, they’ve found favorable matchups to win four of them, but might mix things up as the season goes on.

item.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel blames 1 thing for defensive struggles during Bears game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Patriots’ Mike Vrabel blames 1 thing for defensive struggles during Bears game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots were battling some injuries on their offensive line and elsewhere on the roster, but that misfortune does not fairly describe what went wrong in Thursday’s 30-24 loss versus the Chicago Bears . They wasted opportunities on both sides of the ball. Drake Maye failed to spot an open Efton Chism III and instead threw an interception in the end zone on a pass that was intended for tight end Eli Raridon. There were plenty of defensive mistakes as well. New England was highly vulnerable to the big play during this road matchup, allowing Luther Burden III to record four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown in the first half. Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze also punished the Pats with sizable gains. It is hard to simplify the problem to one area, but head coach Mike Vrabel did highlight his team’s most glaring weakness on defense. “Tackling wasn’t good enough,” he said during the postgame press conference, per MassLive.com’s Mark Daniels. New England made significant strides in fundamental football skills last season, which allowed the squad to post a perfect 8-0 record on the road and reach the Super Bowl. Sloppiness does not travel well, as illustrated by the Patriots’ defensive lapses in Soldier Field. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Burden touchdown was especially hard to stomach. Facing third-and-17 with less than 20 seconds left in the first half, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams linked up with the second-year wideout for a 24-yard score. The Patriots immediately got some revenge courtesy of a bonkers Rhamondre Stevenson TD in the final seconds of the second quarter, but that thrilling play does not excuse the previous mishap. New England cannot gift its opponent momentum at pivotal spots. Missed tackles and 10 penalties made life much easier for Chicago. The Pats will have much to ponder on its trip back home. These blemishes cannot resurface in a Week 8 road game against the winless Miami Dolphins. Related: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel takes the high road on Will Campbell’s controversial penalty in loss to Bears Related: Why Patriots’ Mike Vrabel wasn’t surprised by Cairo Santos calling game with career-long FG
