item.title: LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience in 76ers debut, and he loved every bit of it
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience in 76ers debut, and he loved every bit of it appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LeBron James got a taste of everything Philadelphia fans have to offer in his home debut with the 76ers, and he would not have it any other way . The Sixers fell behind the Cleveland Cavaliers by as many as 29 points in the first half on Thursday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The home crowd let them hear it, booing as Philadelphia went into halftime trailing 69-45 . The mood flipped completely after the break. The Sixers outscored Cleveland 74-37 in the second half and stormed back for a 114-106 win, with the fans back on their feet for the rally. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, James reflected on the night and the reaction from the Philadelphia faithful. “It was everything that I dreamed of and more. We got the boos. That was amazing. We deserved it. And then we had the cheers, and almost blew the roof off this thing tonight, in a good way. It was a hell of a night,” James said. The crowd was loud from the start. Fans erupted before tipoff when James did his signature chalk toss, then turned on the team as the first-half deficit grew. Former Sixer James Harden, now with the Cavaliers, also heard plenty from the stands throughout the night. James had a shaky start himself, committing three of the Sixers’ first five turnovers. He and Tyrese Maxey then sparked the third-quarter surge by pushing the pace in transition. The four-time champion finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists against the franchise he won a title with in 2016. James signed a two-year deal with Philadelphia for the veteran minimum this offseason. Maxey led the Sixers with 32 points, while Joel Embiid added 24. Jaylen Brown, who also made his home debut after his trade from the Boston Celtics , chipped in 21 points. LeBron James got a taste of everything Philadelphia fans have to offer in his home debut with the 76ers, and he would not have it any other way . The Sixers fell behind the Cleveland Cavaliers by as many as 29 points in the first half on Thursday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The home crowd let them hear it, booing as Philadelphia went into halftime trailing 69-45 . The mood flipped completely after the break. The Sixers outscored Cleveland 74-37 in the second half and stormed back for a 114-106 win, with the fans back on their feet for the rally. The crowd was loud from the start. Fans erupted before tipoff when James did his signature chalk toss, then turned on the team as the first-half deficit grew. Former Sixer James Harden, now with the Cavaliers, also heard plenty from the stands throughout the night. James had a shaky start himself, committing three of the Sixers’ first five turnovers. He and Tyrese Maxey then sparked the third-quarter surge by pushing the pace in transition. The four-time champion finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists against the franchise he won a title with in 2016. item.title: Inside Nixa football's fifth straight conference championship
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — The conference title is the first step in Nixa’s ultimate goal. The Eagles (8-1) defeated Glendale 59-14 to secure the Central Ozark Conference East title for the fifth consecutive season on Thursday, Oct. 22. “That’s obviously a goal of ours when we get started,” head coach John Perry said about winning the conference title. “We have great kids and they work hard every single day to get a little better.” Glendale (5-4) jumped ahead first on a 72-yard touchdown pass from Joelle Rover. The star receiver caught a pass from Ryder Spickard near the sideline. He broke a few tackles and was gone for the big score. High school football: Southwest Missouri area Week 9 predictions Nixa turned things around on two key 4th-down calls. The Eagles were stopped at midfield. Instead of punting, the team snapped the ball to Reed Wilson at the up-back position. The fake punt worked beautifully with Wilson breaking multiple tackles down the near sideline. He sprinted into the end zone, tying the game. “I was like, ‘dang, I might go down and be short,’” Wilson said. “I spun off and there was a gap on the left. I was running into the end zone and dang, I did it. I’ve never had a celebration or had to practice it.” On the next offensive possession, Nixa quarterback Adam McKnight tossed a 41-yard touchdown pass across the middle to Carter Mabe. The play came on 4th-and-13, giving Nixa a 14-7 lead. It was a backbreaker for the Falcons and a play that calmed Nixa’s nerves. “It really killed the momentum that they had,” Perry said. “From there, I thought we settled down and played football.” Missouri State: Isaiah Myers leads college football in single-game receiving yards Nixa scored 42 unanswered points leading into the third quarter. McKnight threw a second deep touchdown pass to Mabe. He also rushed for three touchdowns, including a 60-yard scamper. Jax Adams added a long rushing score, too. Xzaevion Manous closed the game with a late touchdown, too. Jonah Fields also added a new career-long 54-yard field goal. Midway through the third quarter, Glendale scored a 55-yard passing touchdown from Spickard to Rover. The night belonged to Wilson. With a fake punt for a touchdown, he rushed for over 80 yards. Entering this game, Wilson had zero carries. Nixa wanted to build depth in case anything happened to starting back Adams. “Reed is an outstanding football player that we’ve been practicing on offense,” Perry said. “Reed is phenomenal. He is a great defensive player and he’s probably top five in the state in tackles. He can come over there and do that, too.” It wasn't the successful night Wilson expected. The defensive back leads Nixa in tackles. He shines on the defensive side of the ball. In the regular-season finale, his offensive skills took center stage, showing his versatility could play a role when the playoffs begin next week. “The punt helped get rid of the nerves. That was my first carry of the season,” Wilson said. “I did just like we practiced.

item.title: Man United hold secret meeting with Antonio Conte after Como disaster, Italian has made his demands clear
item.description: Man United hold secret meeting with Antonio Conte after Como disaster, Italian has made his demands clear After the humbling away to Como in the Champions League, it is clear that the job is far too big for Michael Carrick. After masterminding a stunning turnaround in the second half of last season that eventually got him the permanent role, the current head coach has failed to inspire the team to do even the basics this term. Statistics have shown how woeful the Red Devils have been without the ball, and that was on full display in Italy on Wednesday. Players refused to run, there was no coordinated press, and the tactical calls were bizarre to say the least. Bruno Fernandes even called out the former United midfielder for his flawed in-game approach after the 4-1 defeat. INEOS are reportedly looking at alternatives, with recruitment chief Christopher Vivell pushing for compatriot Julian Nagelsmann, while the director of football wants a Premier League-proven name . United hold late meeting with Antonio Conte Eddie Howe seems to be the favoured choice due to his attractive brand of football and approach to work. However, there is a far more entertaining name on the club’s radar. Antonio Conte, a Premier League winner with Chelsea, could come in and whip the squad back into shape. However, his aggressive approach could lead him to clash with the INEOS hierarchy. This explains the reluctance. However, La Repubblica have claimed that United still got in touch with the Italian’s entourage after the Como result, and the meeting lasted well into the night. The former Napoli boss made a couple of clear-cut demands, which included the right to buy players as per his tactics and the need for a new backroom staff to help him get the job done. “Talks with Conte continued late Wednesday evening: the manager opened up about the possibility of returning to the Premier League, but has set specific conditions. Conte has set two conditions “He is asking for carte blanche on the transfer market and the ability to choose the players who will support him in his new adventure. He wants to influence the team’s construction, identify players who are key to his game, and have trusted collaborators at his side. “In the next few hours, the owners will evaluate the demands, a crucial step in determining whether the dialogue can develop into a concrete negotiation. There has been an opening, but an agreement hasn’t yet been reached.” INEOS have treated managers like head coaches since taking over sporting affairs at the club, and they could be hesitant to let Antonio Conte take over transfer matters after the Erik ten Hag debacle. A new-look coaching staff is relatively easier to pull off, but it will likely include hefty compensation to the current lot. It will be interesting to see if the co-owners bow down to Conte’s demands or choose to go in a different direction. One thing is for certain, Carrick ‘s time is up.

item.title: Justin Barron's Fit With St. Louis Blues As Good As It Gets. "I Just Wanted To Come In, Obviously A Little Bit Of A Clean Slate"
item.description: ST. LOUIS – Justin Barron’s hockey world had just taken a twist that the 24-year-old wasn’t expecting. He was fully committed and in the moment with the Nashville Predators, right in the thick of training camp. Then, things changed, and the defenseman was put on waivers on Sept. 26. The next 24 hours would be filled with uncertainty: would be be claimed by another NHL team; is he heading to Milwaukee of the American Hockey League, or do the Predators keep him? The St. Louis Blues jumped in. They had a rash of injuries and needing help on their blue line. “I just wanted to come in and obviously a little bit of a clean slate,” Barron said after becoming the latest Blues D-man to put up four points , which is a career-high on a goal and three assists Thursday in a 6-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights. “Obviously there's been some injuries here and just try to come into the lineup and prove myself.” Barron, who carries a $1.575 million cap hit in the final year of his contract before becoming a restricted free agent, had plenty of time to think about things on his drive to St. Louis from Nashville, up I-24 West, then I-57 North to I-64 West. “Obviously it’s a whirlwind, your head’s spinning a little bit,” Barron said. “Talked to my parents, talked to my brother (Morgan, a center for the Winnipeg Jets). A bunch of the guys reached out here. I talked to a couple of them on the way up that I already knew. It was obviously a whirlwind, but like I said, I tried to come in with an open mind and it was a fresh start, a little bit of a fresh opportunity for me. Just trying to make the most of it.” Make the most of it he has most certainly done, and in doing so, it’s pushed 2023 first-round pick Theo Lindstein out of the lineup, so much so, that the Blues assigned the 21-year-old to Springfield of the American Hockey League after the game Thursday. Blues winger Dylan Holloway was one of those players Barron spoke to. “I actually played with JB growing up a little bit,” Holloway said. “... He was such a stud back then, he's a stud now. It was a great pickup for us. He played so good tonight. I was really happy to see him have a big night like that.” But Barron didn’t play right away, needing to get acclimated to the Blues’ system, which seems to fit quite nicely for the first-round pick (No. 25) in the 2020 NHL Draft. Blues winger Dylan Holloway was one of those players Barron spoke to. “I actually played with JB growing up a little bit,” Holloway said. “... He was such a stud back then, he's a stud now. It was a great pickup for us. He played so good tonight. But once he jumped into the lineup in the fourth game, the home opener against the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 8, Barron hasn’t come out of the lineup. “I feel good,” said Barron, who has a goal and four assists in seven games. “I've feel like I’m just trying to build my game since I got here. The guys on the team have helped me a lot, just get comfortable. I feel like I'm a part of this team. It was a good, full effort for our team tonight to play a full 60 minutes here at home.” Barron was impactful in the game even before he scored a first-period goal with a quality scoring chance or two, with the puck on his stick quite a bit. But he jumped into the hole after recent call-ups Aleksanteri Kaskimaki and Otto Stenberg forechecked the puck back before Kaskimaki hit Barron coming down the slot. He beat Adin Hill by whipping in a shot from the right circle off the far post and in to give the Blues a 2-0 lead at 13:49 of the first period: St. Louis goal! Scored by Justin Barron with 06:11 left in the 1st. Assisted by Aleksanteri Kaskimaki and Otto Stenberg. STL: 2 | VGK: 0 #VGKvsSTL #StlBlues #VegasBorn pic.twitter.com/OFZ3bFULIA — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 23, 2026 “I'm not even sure if this was his best game,” Blues coach Jim Montgomery said. “He got points and the puck went in, but every game he seems to have four or five attempts from the blue line. He’s been skating the past couple games on the top pairing with Philip Broberg on his natural right side after getting into the lineup with Colton Parayko playing his offside on the left. None of it matters; he’s playing well these days, right or left. “Obviously it showed up for me on the scoresheet (Thursday), but it really felt like everyone on the team played really well tonight,” Barron said. ‘It felt like one of the first games since I’ve gotten here that we played a full 60 minutes. I think a ton of guys played really well tonight. “I think sometimes you can get lucky with some opportunities, someone believing in you. I think at a certain point, it’s up to you to try and make the most of it and really grab that opportunity. That’s what I’m trying to do here.” The Blues play a more aggressive style with their defensemen allowing them to jump in and pinch in the offensive zone, and as an offensive defenseman, Barron is quite adept to that, which allows him to have the success he’s having. When Barron is on the ice, the Blues have scored seven goals for and two against at 5-on-5, according to naturalstattrick.com . “I think it’s just trying to play free,” Barron said. “One thing I really like about the team here is kind of the style they play with how aggressive the D are in the offensive zone. I think that part also made the transition a bit easier for me.” Montgomery said, “Yeah, I mean, outside of your Crosbys, your Brett Hulls, you know, most people it takes the right fit. The right city sometimes, the right culture, the right teammates, the right linemates. For him, I don't know exactly what it is, but certainly he's really comfortable. He seems comfortable since the first practice.” Who knows how long this will last, or what will happen when the Blues get Logan Mailloux (hand injury) and/or Tyler Tucker (knee injury) back. Can Barron’s hot run continue? It will certainly make for some interesting roster decisions. But in the meantime, the Blues plan on riding what Barron can give them and cross that bridge when it’s necessary. And Barron will still live day by day and hope for the best. “I’m still in the hotel. It’s been good,” Barron said. “There’s a couple other guys in there with me, which is nice. We’ve done a little car-pooling and stuff. Been going to dinners with some of the guys, it’s been great.” For action-packed issues, access to the entire magazine archive and a free issue, subscribe to The Hockey News at THN.com/free . Embiid and James are not only the most well-known players on a star-studded roster. They are also the lone Eastern Conference teammates to rank among the top 10 NBA players in projected earnings this season when factoring in salary and endorsements, according to Forbes. So far in his career, Embiid hasn’t led the 76ers past the second round of the playoffs. item.content:encoded: Philadelphia 76ers' LeBron James plays during an NBA basketball game Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, in Philadelphia. James is the fourth highest-paid NBA player this season when factoring salaries and off-court earnings, according to Forbes. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum) Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved At 7:10 pm Thursday night, public address announcer Matt Cord introduced LeBron James, the first time the NBA’s all-time leading scorer had heard his name called for a regular season home game as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. Cord, who came out of retirement when the 76ers signed James this summer, then introduced Joel Embiid, the franchise’s cornerstone since he was selected third overall in the 2014 draft. Embiid and James are not only the most well-known players on a star-studded roster. They are also the lone Eastern Conference teammates to rank among the top 10 NBA players in projected earnings this season when factoring in salary and endorsements, according to Forbes. So far in his career, Embiid hasn’t led the 76ers past the second round of the playoffs. Now, with James and former Boston Celtics All-NBA forward Jaylen Brown on the roster, the expectations are soaring for the franchise. Take Thursday night. When the 76ers fell behind the Cleveland Cavaliers by as many as 29 points in the second quarter, the crowd at Xfinity Mobile Arena booed, just like Philadelphia fans are wont to do. But after the 76ers came back and pulled off a 114-106 victory, those same fans sang “Here Come the Sixers,” the team’s longstanding song following wins. “No shade to anybody that’s been here,” Embiid said. “But in the past, a lot of people would have just laid down and tried to move on to the next one.” LeBron James Earns Most Of His Money In Off-Court Deals Embiid and James, both of whom helped fuel the second half rally, have set the bar high for this season. They will also be highly compensated, although nearly all of James’ earnings come from endorsement deals and other business activities. James signed a two-year contract in late July for the veteran’s minimum of just under $8 million total. His salary of less than $3.9 million this season is the lowest of his career and a major pay cut from last season when he made $52.6 million with the Los Angeles Lakers. It is the first time since 2015 that James will earn less than $30 million in salary. Still, Forbes projects James will earn $90 million from endorsements and other business deals this season. When combining his salary and off-court earnings, James is the fourth highest-paid player in the NBA. Embiid, meanwhile, is tenth on the list with projected earnings of $68 million, including $58 million in salary and $10 million in endorsements. It is the fourth consecutive season Embiid has ranked among the top 10 in earnings. Embiid, who has played a combined 96 games in the past three regular seasons, is sixth in the NBA in salary this season, just ahead of Brown, his teammate who is making $57 million. Embiid is owed $62.6 million next season and has a player option for $67.2 million in the 2028-29 season when he turns 35. And Brown is set to make $61 million next season and $64.9 million the following season when he is 32. James, who turns 42 in December, is still going strong in his 24th NBA season. He is the league leader in career points and games played, and he is unmatched when it comes to his financial rewards. LeBron James Ranks Among Top Earners Each Season Since Forbes began publishing on-court and off-court earnings in the 2011-12 season, James ranked among the top two highest-paid players each season until now. James was the highest-paid player for 11 consecutive seasons until last season when he was second behind Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry. Curry is first again this season with estimated earnings of $203.6 million, including NBA-highs of $62.6 million in salary and $141 million in endorsements and off-court deals. James led the league in off-court earnings each year since Forbes began publishing its data until last year when Curry surpassed him. Still, James’ $90 million in estimated off-court earnings this season is the highest of his career. All told, James has made $961 million since the 2011-12 season in off-court earnings, according to Forbes. In 2021, he surpassed $1 billion in career earnings from salary and endorsements, joining Tiger Woods, Floyd Mayweather, Christiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi as the only athletes to earn at least $1 billion while still playing. A year later, Forbes estimated that James had become a billionaire, becoming the first active NBA player to achieve that feat. James currently has a net worth of $1.4 billion. With that wealth comes constant attention and scrutiny, even from President Donald Trump. On Thursday afternoon, Trump criticized James for practicing a golf swing and jump shot during “The Star-Spangled Banner” before Tuesday’s season opener against the New York Knicks. “I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump said in a social media post. “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” Before Thursday’s game, 76ers coach Nick Nurse was asked about Trump’s comments. “I think that goes right in with other outside noise we’ve already had,” Nurse said. “I kind of keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting them to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor. The focus that they’ve had and the intent and all the stuff they’ve had has been excellent.” Celebrities Come Out For LeBron James’ Home Debut In their home debut, the 76ers had Boyz II Men, a famous singing group from Philadelphia, perform the national anthem. And Bernard Hopkins, a Philadelphia native and former professional boxing champion, rang the customary pregame bell. Allen Iverson, the popular point guard who led the 76ers to their last NBA finals appearance in 2001, was also in attendance. “You could really feel it before the game, probably more than ever (since) I’ve been here, for sure,” said Nurse, who is in his fourth season in Philadelphia. “Just the general buzz and all that kind of stuff.” Still, the 76ers started off nothing like the team that defeated the reigning champion Knicks two nights earlier at Madison Square Garden. Midway through the second quarter, James stole the ball from Cavaliers guard James Harden, a former 76ers’ player who was booed each time he touched the ball Thursday. James then dribbled down the court for a breakaway dunk, cutting the Cavaliers’ lead to 54-32. But later in the quarter, the crowd began booing, frustrated with how 76ers were performing. At halftime, the Cavaliers led, 69-45, as the 76ers committed 15 turnovers, five more than they did all of Tuesday night. The 76ers, though, didn’t fold. They started the third quarter on a 10-0 run and never relented. The 76ers took their first lead of the night when Embiid made a jump shot from near the foul line with 6:54 remaining, putting Philadelphia ahead 96-95. They never trailed again, finishing on a 25-11 run. 76ers’ Second Half Comeback Shows Team’s Potential In the second half, the 76ers outscored the Cavaliers by 32 points, made 50% of their field goals and held Cleveland to 36.8% shooting from the floor, including 2 of 14 on 3-pointers. The 76ers only committed two turnovers in the second half and forced the Cavaliers into 15 turnovers. The comeback was a team effort. Guard Tyrese Maxey and Brown had 17 points apiece in the second half, while Embiid had 15 on 5 of 6 field goals and 5 of 7 free throws and James added 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Nurse has vowed the 76ers will be judicious with Embiid’s and James’ playing time this season. Some nights, they will sit, especially when the 76ers have back-to-back games. The franchise understan

item.title: Oilers earn shootout win over Canes in game of the year so far
item.description: EDMONTON, AB - OCTOBER 22: Edmonton Oilers Center Connor McDavid (97) scores a goal in the third period of the Edmonton Oilers game versus the Carolina Hurricanes on October 22, 2026 at Rogers Place in Edmonton, AB. (Photo by Curtis Comeau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl each notched two goals and three assists for five points on a night where they didn’t have to go up against Jordan Staal. Meanwhile, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had the other goal plus the shootout winner, and despite some truly spectacular goals by the Hurricanes including one all-timer from the returning Seth Jarvis, the Carolina Hurricanes fell to the Edmonton Oilers in the shootout, 6-5. This game was set up as the marquee game of the road trip, as the Oilers were 7-1-1 coming in, and that was before it was going to be the first game back for Jarvis, who had missed the first part of the season recovering from offseason shoulder surgery. Nugent-Hopkins also was playing his first game after injury, and the stars shone bright on a night that saw several goals that’ll be seen over and over. The luster was off this game a little with the Canes down two centers in Jordan Staal and Mark Jankowski, and their absence was felt most on the penalty kill. The first period showed just what sort of game this would be, as both teams got rushes right on top of the opposing goaltender, who both stood strong to start. The ice was broken by Draisaitl on the first power play of the night, and done so in three second of said power play. Without Jordan Staal on the ice, the Canes quickly lost the faceoff, and on a set play the puck was won over to McDavid, who passed up to Evan Bouchard. Bouchard shot it from the point at Draisaitl, who easily deflected it by Brandon Bussi. The Canes, though, fought right back on the power play themselves as Jackson Blake finally was rewarded for the hard work he put up during the road trip. Blake took the pass off the faceoff win, drove to the net and delivered the puck over to Shayne Gostisbehere. Gostisbehere shot it, and Blake was out front of the net to slam home the rebound, tying the score at one. View Link The second period would start quickly for Carolina, as some hard work by Sebastian Aho led to him racing past some Oilers defenders, getting a breakaway, and scoring via the five-hole on Devon Levi. View Link Edmonton wouldn’t trail for long as they would once again get a chance on the power play, and thanks to a shot by the returning Nugent-Hopkins they were able to tie it at two. From there, though, the Canes took over the period. About seven minutes after the Oilers evened it up, Seth Jarvis announced to Canes fans and the NHL that he not only was back, he was feeling great with the shoulder finally repaired after two years. item.content:encoded: EDMONTON, AB - OCTOBER 22: Edmonton Oilers Center Connor McDavid (97) scores a goal in the third period of the Edmonton Oilers game versus the Carolina Hurricanes on October 22, 2026 at Rogers Place in Edmonton, AB. (Photo by Curtis Comeau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl each notched two goals and three assists for five points on a night where they didn’t have to go up against Jordan Staal. Meanwhile, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had the other goal plus the shootout winner, and despite some truly spectacular goals by the Hurricanes including one all-timer from the returning Seth Jarvis, the Carolina Hurricanes fell to the Edmonton Oilers in the shootout, 6-5. This game was set up as the marquee game of the road trip, as the Oilers were 7-1-1 coming in, and that was before it was going to be the first game back for Jarvis, who had missed the first part of the season recovering from offseason shoulder surgery. Nugent-Hopkins also was playing his first game after injury, and the stars shone bright on a night that saw several goals that’ll be seen over and over. The luster was off this game a little with the Canes down two centers in Jordan Staal and Mark Jankowski, and their absence was felt most on the penalty kill. The first period showed just what sort of game this would be, as both teams got rushes right on top of the opposing goaltender, who both stood strong to start. The ice was broken by Draisaitl on the first power play of the night, and done so in three second of said power play. Without Jordan Staal on the ice, the Canes quickly lost the faceoff, and on a set play the puck was won over to McDavid, who passed up to Evan Bouchard. Bouchard shot it from the point at Draisaitl, who easily deflected it by Brandon Bussi. The Canes, though, fought right back on the power play themselves as Jackson Blake finally was rewarded for the hard work he put up during the road trip. Blake took the pass off the faceoff win, drove to the net and delivered the puck over to Shayne Gostisbehere. Gostisbehere shot it, and Blake was out front of the net to slam home the rebound, tying the score at one. View Link The second period would start quickly for Carolina, as some hard work by Sebastian Aho led to him racing past some Oilers defenders, getting a breakaway, and scoring via the five-hole on Devon Levi. View Link Edmonton wouldn’t trail for long as they would once again get a chance on the power play, and thanks to a shot by the returning Nugent-Hopkins they were able to tie it at two. From there, though, the Canes took over the period. About seven minutes after the Oilers evened it up, Seth Jarvis announced to Canes fans and the NHL that he not only was back, he was feeling great with the shoulder finally repaired after two years. It was another breakaway chance, and he just put on a clinic with a goal that will be on his highlight reel for the rest of his career. View Link As the second wound down, the Canes continued their push and showed off their skill with an incredible goal. Nikolaj Ehlers grabbed the puck behind the net and feathered a perfect pass over to Logan Stankoven, even using the goal post to feed it right onto his stick. Stankoven banged it home and took a 4-2 lead into the locker room. View Link The Canes unfortunately let the Oilers back into the game in the third period by doing the thing you can’t do against this team—give that top line room to operate. The first goal came as Aho made an unfortunate gamble in the neutral zone where he was trying to get another breakaway chance. That gamble allowed Edmonton to enter the zone with an odd man rush, and when the Canes overcompensated to try and separate Draisaitl from the puck behind the net, he fed a perfect pass over to McDavid all alone. Bussi had no chance, and it was 4-3. Shortly thereafter Sean Walker was sent to the box for a slash, and for the third time Edmonton’s Power Play made Carolina pay, and this one was Draisaitl off a feed from McDavid. Less than three minutes in, the score was tied at four. The Canes tightened up the rest of the period, however, and were able to keep the Oilers off the board. Then an unlikely hero, Juuso Välimäki would come in and off his first NHL goal since December 2024, give the Canes a lead. The play was thanks to a great keep in by Gostisbehere who managed to keep the speeding puck inside the blue line, and the pass went over to Martinook. Martinook fed the open Välimäki for the shot and score. View Link Unfortunately, being down with two minutes left in the game meant the Oilers could go with the empty net and six skaters, two of which were the Draisaitl and McDavid pairing. One puck went in the net but did so as the officials were calling it being touched with an Oilers high stick. Unfortunately a few seconds later, McDavid would feather a pass in the zone that would deflect off Jesperi Kotkaniemi’s skate and past Bussi on the worst goal he let in on the night. Hats would rain down as fans thought it was off Draisaitl for his third, but the replays clearly showed it was off Kotkaniemi’s skate. Both teams would get chances in overtime with both goalies making some good saves. In the shootout, Bussi managed to stop McDavid and Draisaitl, but couldn’t stop the third shooter in Nugent-Hopkins. Meanwhile, Gostisbehere, Andrei Svechnikov, and Jarvis all were blanked by Levi, and the Oilers skated away with the extra point. Seven Hurricanes in total would get a point on the night, with Jordan Martinook joining Aho with two by assisting on two goals. Carolina will finish the State Fair Road Trip in Saint Louis on Saturday Night, and they’ll do so without a practice on Friday, then finally come home to play four of their last six in Raleigh before heading out to Finland.

item.title: Aaron Boone Goes Against Hal Steinbrenner Comments On Yankees Failure
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 08: Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks back to the dugout after making a pitching change in the ninth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Yankee Stadium on September 08, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. The New York Yankees defeated the Colorado Rockies 5-3. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) Getty The New York Yankees have a tough offseason ahead of them with many major MLB questions for the roster. Pitching looks great, but the offense badly failed the Yankees in the postseason. Both manager Aaron Boone and owner Hal Steinbrenner spoke to the media this week about the disappointing elimination and goals for next season. Steinbrenner seemingly blamed various hitters for the team’s failure. Boone dropped a quote that fully went against that and said it indicates poor leadership to pass blame: “That’s not leadership. That’s me giving red meat to people that want to be upset with somebody.” Yankees fans took note of Boone and Steinbrenner having different philosophies about how to deal with failure. Steinbrenner’s comments implied hitters Jazz Chisholm Jr and Trent Grisham didn’t play up to par. Both men are free agents and expected to be on other teams next season to see Hal passing the blame easier. Boone didn’t want to blame any players and felt it was out of line to throw any individuals under the bus. Leadership was a huge concern for the Yankees this season, especially with captain Aaron Judge injured for most of the year. Steinbrenner and Boone not being on the same page is not the best sign for this partnership moving forward. What Hal Steinbrenner Said That Aaron Boone Disagreed With The end of season press conference for Steinbrenner featured him fully blaming the offense. Steinbrenner said that the hitters underperformed against the Tampa Bay Rays , but most teams have suffered the same fate against the top AL team. The following comments showed Steinbrenner stating the players deserved more blame than Boone or the front office: “The offense had a big part of why we — and I don’t mind saying it — didn’t get to where we strive to get every year,” Steinbrenner said . “That was during the whole year. In the postseason, if you look at their performance against the two starting Boston pitchers and their performance against probably all of the Rays’ pitchers, it was just not good. I don’t know how else to put it. And if you don’t score runs, you’re not going to win.” Steinbrenner also said the offense could have been better against the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series. The Yankees dominating the Wild Card series makes Steinbrenner’s comments a bit stranger to take there. Hal Steinbrenner Received Yankees Fan Backlash The back cover of the New York Daily News showed an edited photo of Steinbrenner pointing to pass the blame to Chisholm and Grisham. Yankees fans were upset with GM Brian Cashman for not making any noteworthy new additions last offseason. The back page: I BLAME YOU Ha

item.title: Rangers Deliver ‘Uncharacteristic’ Performance In Loss To Maple Leafs
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images The New York Rangers suffered a 5-4 defeat at the hands of the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday night, losing their identity in the process. Leading into Thursday night’s game, the Rangers had prided themselves on playing a well-structured defensive game that brought them early-season success, helping them weather the storm without Igor Shesterkin, who suffered a season-ending injury on Oct. 9. The Blueshirts put out one of their more sound and steady defensive performances of the season on Monday night, en route to a decisive 5-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks. However, the Rangers were unable to carry that performance to Toronto, as they were under siege from the opening puck drop, with Easton Cowan scoring a goal less than two minutes into the contest. “It was a little bit of a track meet,” Adam Fox said of the flow of the game. A track meet is a good way to describe the flow of the game. Both teams continued to trade high-quality scoring chances and goals, which is not how the Rangers had secured their seven victories this season. New York gave up a season-high 35 shots, and despite hanging around in the game with goals from Mika Zibanejad, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Tye Kartye, and Alexis Lafrenière, their faulty defensive play continued to put them in a hole throughout the contest and ultimately did them in. In the final minute, with the score tied 4-4, the Rangers’ defense broke down in their own zone, leading to the game-winning goal from Troy Stecher with 26.3 seconds remaining. "We get beat twice going around the net, and then we lose our ice balance,” Sullivan said on Toronto’s game-winning goal. “We left the whole far side of the rink open.” Dylan Garand, who gave up five goals in a game for the first time in his young NHL career, made a total of 30 saves and was praised by Sullivan for giving the Rangers “a chance,” despite not looking his sharpest on some of the Maple Leafs' goals. Sullivan pointed toward the Rangers’ lack of defensive structure for their downfall in Toronto, something he believes was “uncharacteristic of this group,” given the well-structured identity they have been trying to build and have shown for much of the season thus far. “I just didn’t like our overall game,” Sullivan said. “We weren’t stiff enough. “We didn't play with the structure that we need to play with. You know the types of chances we gave up were high. You know we got some chances at the other end, but it was for me it was a loose game. It's not a game conducive to winning.” The Rangers will be back in action on Saturday night against the Ottawa Senators, hoping to bounce back.

item.title: Hamilton sparks laughter with 'slow down' advice to soon-to-be F1 champion Antonelli
item.description: Lewis Hamilton sparked laughter during the FIA press conference ahead of the United States Grand Prix with a cheeky response when asked whether he had any advice for Kimi Antonelli . The seven-time world champion then turned serious, praising the young Italian for his performances and attitude throughout the season. Hamilton was asked whether he had any advice for Antonelli, who replaced him at Mercedes following his move to Ferrari last year. The Italian has enjoyed a strong season, regularly competing towards the front of the grid and establishing himself as one of the most promising young drivers in Formula 1 . The Briton initially responded with just two words: "Slow down," prompting laughter from those present in the press conference. Hamilton then made it clear that Antonelli does not need any guidance from him, highlighting the Italian's talent, composure and approach to racing: "No, I don't know. He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year and also last year, but particularly this year, just his talent and his ability, his calmness and approach, but he's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. "I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers, even with you guys. And it's great to see him and the team excel. You know, if it's not my team, I'd always say I'd always want to see my own team do well." Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Antonelli could clinch his first F1 world title in Austin Antonelli heads into the United States Grand Prix with his first opportunity to clinch the championship. The Mercedes driver holds a commanding 102-point advantage over team-mate George Russell, having claimed eight victories this season. With six Grands Prix remaining on the official calendar, the Italian could become the youngest world champion in F1 history this weekend. However, a victory at the Circuit of the Americas alone would not be enough. The 20-year-old must win Sunday's race, with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton no higher than fifth. Those results would give Antonelli an unassailable advantage with five races remaining. Should Antonelli achieve that feat, he would break Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. The German secured his maiden title with Red Bull in 2010 at the age of 23, while Antonelli could claim his first championship at just 20. He would also become the first Italian driver to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

item.title: Derbyshire Tour de France Femmes route revealed
item.description: The route will see cyclysts passing over the famous Snake Pass route [BBC] Some of Derbyshire's most challenging roads and recognisable landscapes will feature on the route of the Tour de France Femmes when the race comes to the UK for the first time in 2027. Organisers have confirmed Stage 2 of the race will pass through the Peak District on 31 July as riders travel from Manchester to Sheffield. The 154.4km (95.9-mile) stage includes almost 3,000m (9,843ft) of climbing and will take competitors over both Winnats Pass and Snake Pass. Hope and Ladybower Reservoir have also been chosen as sprint locations. Detailing the route on its website, Derbyshire County Council said: "With challenging terrain, dramatic landscapes and iconic climbs, the route will test the world's best riders as they race through the heart of the Peak District. "From historic market towns and picturesque villages (including New Mills, Whaley Bridge, Buxton, Tideswell, Bradwell, Hope, Castleton, Chapel-en-le-Frith, Glossop), to some of Britain's most celebrated cycling roads, the stage has been designed to deliver exciting racing while showcasing the very best that Derbyshire has to offer." Snake Pass is one of Derbyshire's highest roads, which has been at the centre of long-running concerns over landslips, closures and repair costs. Council leaders recently warned that active landslips surrounding Snake Pass could cost more than £100m to investigate and repair. Charlotte Hill, the authority's cabinet member for highways, said the provisional estimate was "beyond our means and why we continue to lobby for more funding" . The road has recently been subject to engineering works and investigations linked to a series of landslips that have affected parts of the route. Leaders say however that they are confident the route can host the race safely. Derbyshire County Council leader Alan Graves said hosting the race was "a big win for Derbyshire". "The best female cyclists in the world are coming here, and they'll face climbs that local riders know only too well," he said. "Winnats Pass and Snake Pass will test anyone. "A global TV audience will see Derbyshire at its best. That brings visitors, and visitors bring money into our pubs, cafés and B&Bs." He acknowledged the event would bring some disruption, with road closures required along the route. "We're working with partners and communities now so there are no surprises, and we'll keep people updated as plans firm up," he said. The Tour de France Femmes will begin in Leeds on 30 July 2027 before crossing the Pennines and finishing in Manchester. The following day, riders will head through Derbyshire and the Peak District before a stage finish in Sheffield. Britain will also become the first country outside France to host the Grand Départs of both the men's and women's Tours in the same year, with the men's race beginning in Edinburgh. The British stages of the women's race will conclude in London on 1 August. Listen to BBC Radio Derb
item.content:encoded: The route will see cyclysts passing over the famous Snake Pass route [BBC] Some of Derbyshire's most challenging roads and recognisable landscapes will feature on the route of the Tour de France Femmes when the race comes to the UK for the first time in 2027. Organisers have confirmed Stage 2 of the race will pass through the Peak District on 31 July as riders travel from Manchester to Sheffield. The 154.4km (95.9-mile) stage includes almost 3,000m (9,843ft) of climbing and will take competitors over both Winnats Pass and Snake Pass. Hope and Ladybower Reservoir have also been chosen as sprint locations. Detailing the route on its website, Derbyshire County Council said: "With challenging terrain, dramatic landscapes and iconic climbs, the route will test the world's best riders as they race through the heart of the Peak District. "From historic market towns and picturesque villages (including New Mills, Whaley Bridge, Buxton, Tideswell, Bradwell, Hope, Castleton, Chapel-en-le-Frith, Glossop), to some of Britain's most celebrated cycling roads, the stage has been designed to deliver exciting racing while showcasing the very best that Derbyshire has to offer." Snake Pass is one of Derbyshire's highest roads, which has been at the centre of long-running concerns over landslips, closures and repair costs. Council leaders recently warned that active landslips surrounding Snake Pass could cost more than £100m to investigate and repair. Charlotte Hill, the authority's cabinet member for highways, said the provisional estimate was "beyond our means and why we continue to lobby for more funding" . The road has recently been subject to engineering works and investigations linked to a series of landslips that have affected parts of the route. Leaders say however that they are confident the route can host the race safely. Derbyshire County Council leader Alan Graves said hosting the race was "a big win for Derbyshire". "The best female cyclists in the world are coming here, and they'll face climbs that local riders know only too well," he said. "Winnats Pass and Snake Pass will test anyone. "A global TV audience will see Derbyshire at its best. That brings visitors, and visitors bring money into our pubs, cafés and B&Bs." He acknowledged the event would bring some disruption, with road closures required along the route. "We're working with partners and communities now so there are no surprises, and we'll keep people updated as plans firm up," he said. The Tour de France Femmes will begin in Leeds on 30 July 2027 before crossing the Pennines and finishing in Manchester. The following day, riders will head through Derbyshire and the Peak District before a stage finish in Sheffield. Britain will also become the first country outside France to host the Grand Départs of both the men's and women's Tours in the same year, with the men's race beginning in Edinburgh. The British stages of the women's race will conclude in London on 1 August. Listen to BBC Radio Derby on Sounds and follow BBC Derby on Facebook , on X , or on Instagram . Send your story ideas to eastmidsnews@bbc.co.uk or via WhatsApp on 0808 100 2210. item.title: Barcelona v Real Madrid tension is building and El Clasico can light a furious fuse
item.description: One regular day of LaLiga, that’s all they are asking for. It did not require fluent Spanish to understand the gravity of Real Madrid ’s ‘Comunicado Oficial’ last Friday afternoon. A press release containing mention of Javier Tebas , the LaLiga president, alongside Joseph Goebbels and the “ministro de Propaganda del régimen nazi” signalled a drastic escalation in their long-running dispute with the Spanish league and that tensions with rivals Barcelona had reached a peak ahead of this weekend’s Clasico at Camp Nou. In the statement, Real Madrid demanded Tebas to resign after he compared the club’s criticism of referees through their in-house TV channel to “propaganda techniques” used by the Nazis during the second world war. The 15-time Champions League winners called the language used by Tebas “deeply offensive” and “morally repugnant” . Tebas, in turn, issued his second lengthy social media post of the day in which he largely doubled down in accusing Real Madrid of “intimidation” and seeking to “destroy” the Spanish league. Barcelona, unsurprisingly, also had their say as club president Joan Laporta criticised Real Madrid for “constantly attacking” LaLiga. Laporta also praised Tebas for being a “counter’ to Madrid’s accusations, which will have done little to dampen the fire building at the Bernabeu. The Madrid supporters had their say during last weekend’s home win over Sevilla, unveiling a banner that played on a LaLiga marketing slogan with the message: “It’s not football, it’s Tebas and Negreira”. Once again, the Negreira case is likely to feature prominently as Barcelona host Real Madrid in El Clasico this weekend. Real Madrid have demanded a “full clarification” as to why payments of €7.3m (£6.5m) from Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira , the former vice-president of the Spanish football federation’s technical committee of referees, were made between 2001 and 2018. Earlier this month Real Madrid sent Uefa a “50,000-page” dossier of documents which they say relate to the “integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system”. Barcelona and Negreira deny wrongdoing and were cleared by Uefa investigators in 2023. Laporta said the payments related to consultancy work and providing reports on referees – but Real Madrid president Florentino Perez ramped up the pressure in May by accusing Barcelona of “stealing” seven league titles from his club. Relations between the historic rivals are usually fraught but they took a further turn when Barcelona finally withdrew from the European Super League in February, leaving Real Madrid as the only founding member of the project to remain on board. It’s an interesting time, then, for the first Clasico of the season to roll around, particularly when Camp Nou will also welcome the return of one of its fiercest opponents: Jose Mourinho . Prepare for ‘war’? It’s been 15 years since Barcelona and Real Madrid’s modern rivalry arguably reached its peak: when El Clasico offered the contrast
item.content:encoded: One regular day of LaLiga, that’s all they are asking for. It did not require fluent Spanish to understand the gravity of Real Madrid ’s ‘Comunicado Oficial’ last Friday afternoon. A press release containing mention of Javier Tebas , the LaLiga president, alongside Joseph Goebbels and the “ministro de Propaganda del régimen nazi” signalled a drastic escalation in their long-running dispute with the Spanish league and that tensions with rivals Barcelona had reached a peak ahead of this weekend’s Clasico at Camp Nou. In the statement, Real Madrid demanded Tebas to resign after he compared the club’s criticism of referees through their in-house TV channel to “propaganda techniques” used by the Nazis during the second world war. The 15-time Champions League winners called the language used by Tebas “deeply offensive” and “morally repugnant” . Tebas, in turn, issued his second lengthy social media post of the day in which he largely doubled down in accusing Real Madrid of “intimidation” and seeking to “destroy” the Spanish league. Barcelona, unsurprisingly, also had their say as club president Joan Laporta criticised Real Madrid for “constantly attacking” LaLiga. Laporta also praised Tebas for being a “counter’ to Madrid’s accusations, which will have done little to dampen the fire building at the Bernabeu. The Madrid supporters had their say during last weekend’s home win over Sevilla, unveiling a banner that played on a LaLiga marketing slogan with the message: “It’s not football, it’s Tebas and Negreira”. Once again, the Negreira case is likely to feature prominently as Barcelona host Real Madrid in El Clasico this weekend. Real Madrid have demanded a “full clarification” as to why payments of €7.3m (£6.5m) from Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira , the former vice-president of the Spanish football federation’s technical committee of referees, were made between 2001 and 2018. Earlier this month Real Madrid sent Uefa a “50,000-page” dossier of documents which they say relate to the “integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system”. Barcelona and Negreira deny wrongdoing and were cleared by Uefa investigators in 2023. Laporta said the payments related to consultancy work and providing reports on referees – but Real Madrid president Florentino Perez ramped up the pressure in May by accusing Barcelona of “stealing” seven league titles from his club. Relations between the historic rivals are usually fraught but they took a further turn when Barcelona finally withdrew from the European Super League in February, leaving Real Madrid as the only founding member of the project to remain on board. It’s an interesting time, then, for the first Clasico of the season to roll around, particularly when Camp Nou will also welcome the return of one of its fiercest opponents: Jose Mourinho . Prepare for ‘war’? It’s been 15 years since Barcelona and Real Madrid’s modern rivalry arguably reached its peak: when El Clasico offered the contrast of Pep Guardiola and Jose Mourinho and their clash of styles, the two best managers in the world on the touchline as much of a draw than the best players in the world on the pitch in Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Mourinho would prepare his players for “war”, a tactic that will not be forgotten at Camp Nou and could be deployed again now as Real Madrid attempted to halt a Barcelona side who have scored 50 goals in their first 12 matches of the season. Hansi Flick’s team won their first 11 in a row, until Tuesday’s Champions League defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, and lead Real Madrid by six points in LaLiga. Mourinho can’t afford another defeat now. Real Madrid and Barcelona’s clashes in the 2010/11 season saw the drama of the Clasico reach a peak (Getty) Mourinho will take charge of his first Clasico as Real Madrid boss since leaving the club in 2013 (Reuters) It did not take Mourinho long on his return to Spain, however, to play into the narrative that Real Madrid have up against something bigger than just Barcelona. Having suffered their first defeat of the season at Real Betis, Mourinho arrived at his press conference following the heated 2-1 derby defeat at Atletico Madrid holding printouts of the “two clear red cards” Diego Simeone’s team should have received in the first half. Given the attention Mourinho looked to draw towards the two incidents – a studs-up challenge from Cristian Romero on Jude Bellingham ’s knee and Lee Kang-in catching Federico Valverde on his ankle – any late challenges in the Clasico which Real Madrid feel are dealt with too leniently or too strongly could be the match that sparks the dynamite. In between the controversy, it’s easy to forget what the selling point of El Clasico really should be about: the stars. The Premier League may be the most dominant domestic competition in the world but it does not have a fixture that comes close to matching the individual talent on display when Kylian Mbappe faces Lamine Yamal and the midfield battle is decided by either Bellingham or Rodri. The prospect of Yamal enjoying a potential crowning moment at Camp Nou, a night before the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London and in front of a Real Madrid side who were left seething by Vinicius Jr missing out on the award two years ago, adds another delicious storyline into the mix. But the sharp edge to world football’s biggest club fixture is back as well.

item.title: The unfashionable World Series that could determine baseball’s future
item.description: For fans of the underdog, this is the World Series for you. The Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Yankees, New York Mets and all of baseball’s other biggest spenders have fallen by the wayside, leaving the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays as the last two teams standing. Two of the sport’s more unfashionable franchises are both trying to win the World Series for the very first time and not since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Kansas City Royals, has such a match-up occurred. It means that by the time 2026 Fall Classic completes its best-of-seven series next weekend, there will only be four of MLB ’s 30 franchises never to have hoisted the Commissioner’s Trophy aloft. The Seattle Mariners – who are the only team never to have even played in a World Series – Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and this year’s losers will make up the unfortunate quartet. The Tampa Bay Rays won the American League and are hoping to triumph in the World Series for the first time in their history (Getty) This year’s clash makes a refreshing change in a sport where money usually talks, as evidenced by the Dodgers – with the highest payroll in the MLB – winning back-to-back titles and seeming destined to become the first team to pull off a three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees until they ran into Milwaukee-shaped juggernaut in the National League Championship Series, and were swept 4-0, Milwaukee, a city of fewer than 600,000 people in the rural state of Wisconsin, is MLB’s smallest media market and the Brewers rank 19th when it comes to payroll. Remarkably, the Rays are 28th in payroll, with only the Cleveland Guardians – who they beat in the American League Championship Series – and the Miami Marlins spending less on salary. The two World Series participants have a combined payroll of barely over half that of the Dodgers and not since 1991 have both pennant winners been among the bottom 50 per cent of the league in player spending. They are two analytically-driven franchises punching above their weight thanks to smart management and superb player scouting. So while in one respect this is a surprise World Series match-up, in another it very much isn’t. They both had the best regular-season record in their respective leagues (Brewers with 103 wins in the NL, Rays with 98 wins in the AL) as they were able to maintain their excellence over MLB’s bloated 162-game campaign. Flame-throwing Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers is the best pitcher in baseball (Getty) And while they might not be able to overpay in order to acquire other teams’ best talent, they have done a remarkable job at developing their own. item.content:encoded: For fans of the underdog, this is the World Series for you. The Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Yankees, New York Mets and all of baseball’s other biggest spenders have fallen by the wayside, leaving the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays as the last two teams standing. Two of the sport’s more unfashionable franchises are both trying to win the World Series for the very first time and not since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Kansas City Royals, has such a match-up occurred. It means that by the time 2026 Fall Classic completes its best-of-seven series next weekend, there will only be four of MLB ’s 30 franchises never to have hoisted the Commissioner’s Trophy aloft. The Seattle Mariners – who are the only team never to have even played in a World Series – Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and this year’s losers will make up the unfortunate quartet. The Tampa Bay Rays won the American League and are hoping to triumph in the World Series for the first time in their history (Getty) This year’s clash makes a refreshing change in a sport where money usually talks, as evidenced by the Dodgers – with the highest payroll in the MLB – winning back-to-back titles and seeming destined to become the first team to pull off a three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees until they ran into Milwaukee-shaped juggernaut in the National League Championship Series, and were swept 4-0, Milwaukee, a city of fewer than 600,000 people in the rural state of Wisconsin, is MLB’s smallest media market and the Brewers rank 19th when it comes to payroll. Remarkably, the Rays are 28th in payroll, with only the Cleveland Guardians – who they beat in the American League Championship Series – and the Miami Marlins spending less on salary. The two World Series participants have a combined payroll of barely over half that of the Dodgers and not since 1991 have both pennant winners been among the bottom 50 per cent of the league in player spending. They are two analytically-driven franchises punching above their weight thanks to smart management and superb player scouting. So while in one respect this is a surprise World Series match-up, in another it very much isn’t. They both had the best regular-season record in their respective leagues (Brewers with 103 wins in the NL, Rays with 98 wins in the AL) as they were able to maintain their excellence over MLB’s bloated 162-game campaign. Flame-throwing Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers is the best pitcher in baseball (Getty) And while they might not be able to overpay in order to acquire other teams’ best talent, they have done a remarkable job at developing their own. The Brewers boast the best pitcher in baseball in the form of flame-throwing phenom Jacob Misiorowski, who can reach 105mph with his fastball, is a shoo-in for the NL Cy Young award and will start Game 1 of the World Series on Friday evening, and superstar 22-year-old Venezuelan outfielder Jackson Chourio. Meanwhile, the Rays have the likes of AL MVP candidate Junior Caminero as a hard-hitting third baseman, lights-out closer Bryan Baker and stolen base machine Chandler Simpson. Junior Caminero has had back-to-back 40 homerun seasons for the Tampa Bay Rays (AP) This promises to be a fascinating edition of the Fall Classic although without a traditional big-name franchise in the mix, there is a legitimate fear it may struggle to attract the casual sports fan and could rival the 2023 edition, when the Texas Rangers beat the Arizona Diamondbacks in five games, as the least-watched World Series on record. Let’s hope not as these two teams deserve to have the eyes of the US on them over the next 10 days or so. However, even if it struggles to truly cut through in the crowded sports landscape, this World Series could yet have a huge impact on the very future of baseball. The current Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the players and the league (essentially the contract between the two sides that allows major league baseball to be played) expires on 1 December and there is no new agreement in sight. There will almost certainly be a lockout while the two sides try to hash out a deal and there’s a good chance this delays the start of spring training (baseball’s preseason). The question then becomes whether the labour dispute will bleed into the time when the 2027 season itself should be starting and mean regular-season games have to be sacrificed. This would ultimately cost both sides money, so they will be keen to avoid it, but the 1972 and 1981 seasons were shortened for this reason, 1994 saw the entire postseason cancelled meaning there was no World Series and the most recent lockout in 2022 caused spring training to be abbreviated and opening day pushed back. MLB and the players are locked in a CBA dispute (Getty) The main sticking point of any potential CBA looks set to be the proposal from Major League Baseball and the team owners to introduce a salary cap. Baseball is the only one of North America’s four major sports without a cap and the owners are keen to bring one in to limit payroll spending and stop runaway contract inflation and bidding wars on players. They claim it will create a fairer system for all 30 teams and ensure greater competitive balance by not allowing the big-market franchises to simply outspend their opponents and giving the smaller teams a better chance to retain their stars. There would also be a salary floor, which they say will raise wages for the non-superstar players. By contrast, the players union view the salary cap as a tool to unfairly suppress player compensation and argue that smaller franchises are already capable of beating the big dogs by being smartly run, without the need to artificially reduce spending via an arbitrary cap. They believe the playoffs create enough randomness and competitive parity already and this ‘small-market World Series’ between the Brewers and Rays could hardly have come at a better time from their perspective – weakening the owners’ suggestion that without a cap, only the big-market teams can win. The LA Dodgers’ had won back-to-back World Series before this year (Getty) In response, the league would rightly point to the fact that the last time a small payroll team won before 2026 was the Royals in 2015, meaning this is simply an anomaly. The owners are proposing a hard salary cap of $245.3m and a salary floor of $171.2m for 2027. If that had been in place this year, only 10 of the 30 MLB teams would have been compliant, with eight franchises coming in above the cap and 12 falling below the salary floor. If this is introduced, it will fundamentally change the face of the sport and a long hard winter of negotiations seems inevitable. So, enjoy this unusual World Series. Not only is it two brilliant teams going head to head, it might be the last bit of Major League Baseball action for a while. In fact, it might even determine the future of the entire sport.

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.description: The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday , but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level. item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.title: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’
item.description: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means “It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday. “It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.” Continue reading...

item.description: ‘A player off with really sharp pain is never good news’ Winger forced off 10 minutes into Arsenal’s 2-2 draw Mikel Arteta made no attempt to conceal his concern over the quad injury that forced Bukayo Saka out of Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich , saying it did not “look good at all”. The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot. Continue reading...
